item.title: Atiku to flag off ADC presidential campaign in Sokoto
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), is expected to visit Sokoto on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, to flag off the party’s presidential campaign activities in the state ahead of the 2027 general elections. Atiku is scheduled to arrive at the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport, Sokoto, at 9 a.m., where party supporters, political associates and members of the public are expected to receive him. The Coordinator of the Sokoto State ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Ibrahim Lamido, disclosed this in a statement made available to journalists. According to the statement, the visit is part of the party’s efforts to strengthen its grassroots structures and consolidate support ahead of the 2027 presidential election. It called on party members, supporters and well-meaning residents to turn out in large numbers to welcome the ADC presidential candidate. The statement said the visit would also feature the flag-off of the party’s presidential campaign in Sokoto State at its secretariat, located at No. 1, Ilorin Road, Sokoto. The event is expected to attract party leaders, elected and appointed political office holders, local government and ward executives, mobilisation coordinators, support groups and other stakeholders. Lamido said local government and ward executives had been directed to activate their political structures and mobilise members and supporters across the state. Women and youth organisations, as well as affiliated support groups, were also urged to intensify grassroots mobilisation and participate actively in the event. The campaign council further called on mobilisation coordinators to ensure effective coordination among the party’s structures to guarantee a successful reception and campaign flag-off. Atiku’s visit comes amid increasing political activities and realignments ahead of the 2027 general elections, as political parties step up efforts to expand their support bases. The statement, however, did not provide further details of the presidential candidate’s engagements during the visit. The post Atiku to flag off ADC presidential campaign in Sokoto appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Brewers’ Pat Murphy reveals star-studded afterparty hangs after SNL appearance
item.description: Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Brewers’ Pat Murphy reveals star-studded afterparty hangs after SNL appearance appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Pat Murphy and the Milwaukee Brewers took their World Series celebration to New York for a surprise appearance on “ Saturday Night Live ,” and the Brewers manager ended up rubbing elbows with some Hollywood heavyweights after the show. Murphy, Christian Yelich and Brice Turang crashed the “Weekend Update” segment on Saturday, with the Commissioner’s Trophy in tow. Murphy told Bobby Moynihan’s recurring Drunk Uncle character, “I’m the manager, and that’s kind of like being the drunk uncle of the team.” Murphy skipped the official afterparty, but he still found himself in some star-studded company. Speaking on “The Show” podcast with Joel Sherman and Jon Heyman of the New York Post, Murphy revealed that he spent time with Lorne Michaels, Tom Hanks, Steven Spielberg and J.J. Abrams. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We all went up in Lorne Michaels’ office with Yelich and Turang, and we just sat there,” Murphy said. “Seven of us sat there, no beverages, just sat there and conversed.” Pat Murphy didn't go to the SNL after party but he did get the chance to talk to Tom Hanks, Stephen Spielberg, JJ Abrams and Lorne Michaels. The Show with @Joelsherman1 & @JonHeyman –> https://t.co/oK4vrCuQFY pic.twitter.com/1iat279lYQ — New York Post Sports (@nypostsports) November 4, 2026 Murphy even left Hanks with a souvenir. “I gave Tom Hanks my game hat from the World Series,” Murphy said. “And he said, ‘I’m not taking it off. I’m wearing this. So it’s going to get paint on it. It’s going to get garbage on it. The next time you see it, it’s going to be dirty. I’m not putting it on a shelf.’” Hanks also had a professional reason for keeping an eye on Murphy. “Hanks, he’s going to be a pitching coach in a movie or something like that. So he said he was studying my mannerisms,” Murphy said. “And he goes, ‘Ah, I really didn’t get much from you. You just have the same face for nine innings.’” The conversation also touched on Murphy’s viral comment about the New York Yankees. A hot mic caught Murphy calling them a “horses**t Yankees team” while joking with first baseman Jake Bauers during the on-field celebration after Milwaukee’s title-clinching Game 5 win over the Tampa Bay Rays. Michaels, a big Yankees fan, discussed the moment with Murphy, who made sure to clarify his respect for Aaron Boone . “Aaron Boone, I’ve gotten to know him, and I really, really like him,” Murphy said. It has been quite a week for Murphy, who guided the Brewers to the first World Series championship in franchise history . Related: Brewers manager Pat Murphy explains ‘hors**t Yankees’ comment that went viral after World Series win Related: Pat Murphy gets brutally honest on Brewers’ World Series parade

item.title: Why Aaron Taylor believes Ohio State will bounce back and beat Oregon
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Why Aaron Taylor believes Ohio State will bounce back and beat Oregon appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ohio State fans expected harsh treatment from the College Football Playoff selection committee. Undefeated Florida State was denied entry into the four-team 2023-24 CFP because quarterback Jordan Travis suffered a gruesome, ultimately career-ending leg injury, so the Julian Sayin situation was bound to cost the Buckeyes. Apparently, though, decision-makers used the team’s spotty defensive showing in last Saturday’s 30-18 loss versus USC to explain its No. 12 ranking. CFP selection committee chairman Hunter Yurachek suggested as much on Tuesday night. While there were certainly uncharacteristic lapses in Los Angeles, Ohio State is still allowing only 15.5 points per game. An inexperienced quarterback in Luke Fahey and 11 penalties for 71 yards obviously played big roles in this humbling defeat. Citing a generally brilliant Matt Patricia-engineered defense as the reasoning for the Buckeyes’ standing is interesting, to say the least. Ohio State now has extra motivation to bombard the visiting Oregon Ducks on Saturday afternoon. CBS Sports analyst Aaron Taylor expects the home team to respond after its failed trip to LA . Desperation and track record form the basis of his argument. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Their backs are against the wall,” the Super Bowl 31 champion and two-time All-American offensive lineman said on “Inside College Football.” “If they lose, they’re out, boys. They’ve only given up four touchdown passes all season-long, so yeah they took their lumps last week… but this front seven, when they play at their best against Oregon’s best, from what we’ve seen on tape this year, this thing may not be close.” Ohio State's back is against the wall. 👀 @AaronTaylorCFB believes Ohio State will get the job done against Oregon and it might not be close. #ICF pic.twitter.com/Mkl8fMcF86 — CBS Sports College Football 🏈 (@CBSSportsCFB) November 4, 2026 Ohio State is not inspiring much confidence among the CFP committee, but Taylor effectively sums up why this squad deserves more respect. Furthermore, the Buckeyes have the luxury of playing in Columbus. Fahey should be more comfortable surrounded by thunderous support rather than unsympathetic USC fans. The defense should also be up to task. If head coach Ryan Day can get his players to cut down on the penalties, the squad’s profusion of talent should shine through. Oregon QB Dylan Raiola is coming off a stellar performance versus Northwestern — 71.0 completion percentage, 336 passing yards and three touchdowns — but Ohio State is a different beast, especially in The Horseshoe. Coming off a second loss, the Buckeyes already have plenty incentive to dispatch of the Ducks, but thanks to Hunter Yurachek and his colleagues, they should have a super-sized chip on their shoulder when they take the field. Ope

item.title: NFL Insider urges Vikings to pair Kyler Murray with Jonathan Taylor
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images NFL Insider urges Vikings to pair Kyler Murray with Jonathan Taylor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Vikings sit at a pivotal crossroads, and one major roster splash could elevate their offense from stagnant to lethal. Sports analyst Danny Parkins thinks Minnesota general manager Nolan Teasley needs to land Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor to maximize quarterback Kyler Murray . Murray’s initial stretch under head coach Kevin O’Connell has produced mixed results. Over five appearances, Murray completed 83 of 125 passes for a 66.4% completion rate, throwing three touchdowns and two interceptions while adding 132 rushing yards on 25 carries. Veteran tailback Aaron Jones has carried a heavy burden with 436 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 105 carries, but Minnesota lacks a true power hammer behind him. Parkins noted that Murray played his most efficient football during his Arizona Cardinals tenure alongside James Conner. Conner’s inside-out physicality forced defenses into heavy boxes and gave Murray cleaner passing lanes. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Who should go get Jonathan Taylor ? @DannyParkins weighs in: “The Minnesota Vikings, if they believe in themselves… The thing where Kyler Murray looked most effective, he had James Conner… I think he changes the complexion of Kyler and that whole team.” pic.twitter.com/QxlELdCUoA — First Things First (@FTFonFS1) November 4, 2026 Enter Taylor, who remains one of the premier weapons in the league. Through eight games this season, Taylor has logged 587 rushing yards and eight touchdowns on 140 carries, adding 17 receptions for 178 yards. The Vikings got a firsthand look at that firepower when Taylor gashed their defense for 95 rushing yards and a touchdown on 18 carries at U.S. Bank Stadium. According to reports from Bleacher Report and The Athletic, Minnesota remains among the front-runners monitoring Taylor’s availability before the trade deadline. The asking price will not come cheap, but pairing Taylor with Murray instantly solves Minnesota’s goal-line struggles and unlocks lethal play-action options. If Minnesota truly believes in its championship window, securing a blue-chip talent like Taylor provides the exact spark needed to ignite the playbook.

item.title: Kendrick Perkins sounds off on ‘liability’ Draymond Green after ejection against Suns
item.description: Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images Draymond Green was ejected from the Golden State Warriors’ game against the Phoenix Suns, and Kendrick Perkins has taken the opportunity to call him out. The Golden State Warriors managed a narrow win against the Phoenix Suns on Monday, improving to a 5-3 record. This came despite Draymond Green getting ejected for picking up two technicals in the same passage of play. Green made a questionable foul on big man Khaman Maluach, with Dillon Brooks showing up to have his teammate’s back. This escalated the situation, even as Draymond tried grabbing the Canadian star by the throat. His actions have led to significant criticism, and Kendrick Perkins has now weighed in as well. Kendrick Perkins says Draymond Green has been ‘non-existent’ in basketball terms this season Green has a history of getting involved with ‘extra-curricular’ skirmishes on the court, this isn’t exactly his first offence. Kendrick Perkins isn’t new to calling him out either, the two have a history of getting into very public beef with one another. So when this incident occurred, it was always likely to lead to something. Perkins hasn’t missed his opportunity, calling Green out in some very harsh terms. “Listen, when was the last time we discussed Draymond Green and brought him up for his basketball and not fighting?” Perkins asked on ESPN. “At some point, he has to deliver on the floor. When you look at the start of this season, Draymond Green has been non-existent. “He has done absolutely nothing for the Golden State Warriors. To me, he has been a liability more than an asset. When you look at Steph’s face, yes he’s always going to protect Draymond Green because of their brotherhood… At some point, we have to stop giving Draymond a pass and say, ‘Hey man, when are you going to start producing on the floor?'” Green’s impact has always shown up outside the box score more than anywhere else. The four-time NBA champion may be prone to the occasional outburst, but his importance to the team cannot be denied. Perkins criticising him in this manner could even cause Green to respond and rekindle the feud, too. item.title: 'We cannot rely on him!' - Enzo Maresca issues urgent goalscoring warning to Man City stars as Erling Haaland's streak ends
item.description: Manchester City v Brighton & Hove Albion - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Enzo Maresca has warned Manchester City that they cannot continue to rely solely on Erling Haaland to score their goals this season. The manager issued the clear instruction to his squad after they surrendered top spot in the Premier League following a frustrating weekend defeat against Brighton. City suffer frustrating Brighton defeat Maresca has told his City squad that they must stop relying entirely on Haaland for goals. The Norwegian striker has already scored 13 times across all competitions this season. However, Haaland was unable to find the back of the net as City suffered a 1-0 defeat to Brighton on Saturday. The disappointing result saw Maresca's side knocked off the top of the Premier League table. The blank against Brighton highlighted a potential weakness in the squad. Maresca is now eager to see other players step up and contribute in the final third. Maresca demands goals from elsewhere Speaking ahead of the Champions League clash against RB Leipzig, Maresca discussed the performance of his team's attacking line. The manager stressed the importance of sharing the goalscoring burden across the pitch. "At the same time, we cannot rely on Erling for every game. We need also the rest to score goals," Maresca explained, as quoted by ESPN . "But, again, I think the last game against Brighton was the only game of the season where we didn't score. But, for sure, if Erling is on the pitch we are happy." Haaland remains crucial for City While calling for wider contributions, Maresca was quick to highlight Haaland's immense value to the team. The manager acknowledged that having the prolific forward on the pitch always provides an advantage. The manager said: "For sure, when you have Erling inside the pitch, it's better because he's going to score goals, or you know he's always there close." Champions League test awaits City City will look to bounce back immediately as they turn their attention to European action. They are currently preparing to face Leipzig in Germany on Wednesday night. Maresca's side have made a solid start to the competition, picking up important victories over Porto and AEK Athens . However, Maresca's side did suffer a defeat against Paris Saint-Germain last month. A strong performance against Leipzig will be vital as they aim to regain their momentum and get back to winning ways.

item.title: 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings: LaNorris Sellers is delivering on his talent
item.description: 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings: LaNorris Sellers is delivering on his talent appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a lot of movement early in the season in the 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings, things are starting to settle as the calendar turns to November. Drew Mestemaker is the clear No. 1 QB in this class, even if he ends up going back to school for another year to gain some more experience. Dante Moore, after starting the season as a clear top-five pick, now is surrounded by questions as his college career was cut short. The same, of course, goes for Brendan Sorsby. But there are still some very impressive signal-callers that are rising up the rankings. LaNorris Sellers , after starting the season by falling down the rankings, is now rising back up and playing some of the best football of his South Carolina career . Austin Simmons has been arguably the fastest riser of the season, and he continued that with another strong game on Saturday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Week 10 is one of the biggest slates in recent memory in college football, and there will be plenty of chances for all of these guys to make big statements over the weekend. Heading into that lineup of juicy games, how do the top 10 QBs in the upcoming NFL Draft shake out? 1. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State William Purnell-Imagn Images Last week: 1 Mestemaker got let down by his defense and a few bad decisions of his own on Saturday night, but he still finished with 323 yards and five touchdowns in a crazy 51-49 loss to Iowa State. That’s kind of the story with Mestemaker week in and week out at this point. Mestemaker can make all the throws, he is a great athlete, and all of that is on display every time he takes the field. item.content:encoded: 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings: LaNorris Sellers is delivering on his talent appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After a lot of movement early in the season in the 2027 NFL Draft QB rankings, things are starting to settle as the calendar turns to November. Drew Mestemaker is the clear No. 1 QB in this class, even if he ends up going back to school for another year to gain some more experience. Dante Moore, after starting the season as a clear top-five pick, now is surrounded by questions as his college career was cut short. The same, of course, goes for Brendan Sorsby. But there are still some very impressive signal-callers that are rising up the rankings. LaNorris Sellers , after starting the season by falling down the rankings, is now rising back up and playing some of the best football of his South Carolina career . Austin Simmons has been arguably the fastest riser of the season, and he continued that with another strong game on Saturday. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Week 10 is one of the biggest slates in recent memory in college football, and there will be plenty of chances for all of these guys to make big statements over the weekend. Heading into that lineup of juicy games, how do the top 10 QBs in the upcoming NFL Draft shake out? 1. Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State William Purnell-Imagn Images Last week: 1 Mestemaker got let down by his defense and a few bad decisions of his own on Saturday night, but he still finished with 323 yards and five touchdowns in a crazy 51-49 loss to Iowa State. That’s kind of the story with Mestemaker week in and week out at this point. Mestemaker can make all the throws, he is a great athlete, and all of that is on display every time he takes the field. But his inexperience costs him in a big way once or twice throughout the game, and sometimes that’s enough to cost the Cowboys and their defense the game. 2. Trinidad Chambliss, Ole Miss Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Last week: 2 After a rough day at the office against Texas, Chambliss got back on track on Saturday with a three-touchdown day against Auburn in a 45-15 win. It was nice to see the Rebels lean back into using Chambliss as a runner, as he gashed the Tigers on a number of designed runs and finished with 65 yards and a score on the ground. Now, a big test awaits. Chambliss will welcome Georgia back to Oxford after torching the Bulldogs twice last season, including in the Sugar Bowl to end their season. Kirby Smart’s group will be very hungry, but that might not matter if the senior quarterback is on his game. 3. LaNorris Sellers, South Carolina Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Last week: 4 Sellers threw a pair of interceptions on Saturday, but it’s hard not to be enamored with his physical tools as he continues to marry that with good process as a passer and improved accuracy. Sellers finished with nearly 400 yards of offense and five touchdowns on the road against a very good Oklahoma defense in a 42-25 win, including 96 yards and two scores as a runner. He is one of the most explosive athletes in this class, regardless of position, and the playmaking bag that unlocks was on full display in this game. LANORRIS SELLERS ACCOUNTED FOR 397 YARDS AND 5 TOUCHDOWNS AS SOUTH CAROLINA TOOK DOWN OKLAHOMA. 19/24, 301 PASS YDS, 3 PASS TD, 2 INT, 96 RUSH YDS, 2 RUSH TD Sellers is reminding everyone why he entered the season with top 5 NFL Draft hype. https://t.co/p3W7SKL0HX pic.twitter.com/EgYm7QFzgT — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 1, 2026 Sellers will have to end up in the right situation in the NFL, preferably with an offensive coordinator that will allow him to use his legs and unlock his talent as a playmaker. But if he does, the sky is the limit for him. 4. Darian Mensah, Miami (FL) Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Last week: 3 Mensah and the Miami offense had to bail out a shaky Hurricanes defense on Saturday night in a 38-35 win over North Carolina, and they did just that. The star quarterback finished 22-of-29 with 274 yards and three touchdowns, operating with the same precision, timing and accuracy that has him right in the middle of the Heisman Trophy discussion this season. Mensah also showed off his scrambling ability in this game, which he is capable of but doesn’t like to use often. He finished with 36 yards on the ground, and Miami might need more where that came from if it is going to keep its undefeated season going with a win over Notre Dame. 5. Austin Simmons, Missouri Brett Rojo-Imagn Images Last week: 7 The Missouri offense got off to a bit of a slow start on Saturday in a win over Arkansas, but Simmons’ arm talent was on full display. he finished 20-of-31 with 179 yards and two touchdowns in what ended up as a 34-10 win, but it was his throw of the year candidate that caught the attention of scouts and fans alike online. This throw from Austin Simmons is INSANE pic.twitter.com/vuUVbl32BE — Connor O'Gara (@cjogara) November 1, 2026 Simmons still has some inconsistencies in his game, but he is the real deal from the pocket. There will be plenty of NFL teams willing to take a chance on a player who is willing and able to access all of the throws, even in tight windows, with real velocity and ball placement on a consistent basis. 6. C.J. Carr Notre Dame Bob Donnan-Imagn Images Last week: 5 Carr and Notre Dame kicked it into gear when it mattered on Saturday despite a slow start against Navy, but that was more about the shortcomings of the defense than it was anything about Carr’s performance. But rhetorical fact of the matter is that Carr hasn’t been forced to be uncomfortable all that much this season, and the results were somewhat mixed in the Irish’s loss to BYU. On Saturday, he will surely have to rise up and put the offense on his back at times against No. 1 Miami. 7. Arch Manning, Texas Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Last week: 6 Manning and Texas finally were able to breeze through a game, as they dismantled a Mississippi State team whose season has been derailed by the injury to Kamario Taylor. Manning had a solid, but unspectacular, game, finishing 16-of-20 with 220 yards and three touchdowns. The junior QB’s toughness and grit was on display, as he took a number of big hits but continued to lead the Longhorns offense up and down the field. Now, Manning embarks on one of his toughest stretches of schedule yet. The Longhorns will go on the road to take on a Missouri team with a very good pass rush on Saturday, and then they will head to Death Valley for a date with LSU in Week 11. If he can excel against those two defenses, he could start to rise back up these rankings. 8. Dante Moore, Oregon Ben Lonergan/The Register-Guard / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Last week: 8 Moore will continue holding strong in this spot most likely, as there is a pretty steep tier gap between Manning at seven and Brendan Sorsby at nine. His career in college is very likely over, but Moore still has plenty of arm talent and a lot of good tape in 2025 that teams can go back to. His ability to play with pressure in his face will remain a question all the way up to the draft. 9. Brendan Sorsby Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Last week: 10 Sorsby is in a similar spot to Moore, as some quarterbacks have risen firmly above him while others have fallen far below. It seems unlikely that he will move far from this spot either way over the rest of the season. Of course, how he handles the pre-draft process and addresses his gambling scandal will be key in how high teams are willing to take him. 10. Kenny Minchey, Kentucky Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Last week: NR Minchey makes his debut in these rankings as one of the biggest risers of the season for Will Stein’s resurgent Kentucky program. Minchey nearly beat out C.J. Carr for the starting job at Notre Dame before last season, and this year he is showing why he made that battle so competitive. He conducts the Kentucky offense ver

item.title: Manchester City may have only scratched the surface of Elliot Anderson’s enormous potential
item.description: Manchester City may have only scratched the surface of Elliot Anderson’s enormous potential Elliot Anderson has made a strong start to his Manchester City career. The England international has firmly established himself as a key component of Manchester City’s midfield. His tireless work rate, ability to win duels and quality in possession make Anderson the fulcrum of City’s midfield. However, as impressive as Anderson has been there is a scary thought for Manchester City’s rivals to consider. Anderson has barely scratched the surface of the midfielder he could become. That is an exciting prospect to consider as Enzo Maresca raised this possibility yesterday. Enzo Maresca believes that Elliot Anderson has the ability to play in a more advanced midfield role. Manchester City manager has used Elliot Anderson primarily as a number six in midfield this season. The endless energy that Anderson has makes him a quality number six. Couple this with his quality in possession and his strengths in duels, Anderson is the player for City to build their midfield around. Speaking yesterday, ahead of Manchester City’s Champions League league phase fixture against RB Leipzig, Enzo Maresca explained that Anderson has the ability to play as a number eight in midfield. Maresca believes that Anderson has the ability to arrive in the box and add more goals to his game. He explained: “ I think in this moment he is playing in the position which is best for him. That is a holding midfielder like a six. ” “ No doubt in the future he can be also a number eight and arrive in the box. He has a good pass and also I think he can score some more goals .” “ In this moment I’m trying to know all of them in the right way. It’s just been four months so I need to know them better and they need to know me better. It’s on both sides. But for sure he can be a number eight that arrives inside the box.” Once Elliot Anderson adds more goals and assists to his game he will be the complete midfield weapon for Manchester City. It hasn’t taken long at all for Elliot Anderson to show why Manchester City were so eager to sign him from Nottingham Forest. Anderson has been Manchester City’s standout player alongside Erling Haaland for the 2026-27 season. The fact that the 23-year-old midfielder has cast aside any pressure of the heavy price that City paid to sign him is a credit to him. As Anderson is only 23, it does bode well for how much more he can grow as a player. Elliot Anderson has the potential to add goals and assists to his game. At times, Anderson moves like De Bruyne. Anderson will never be the type of midfielder that De Bruyne was. No player ever will be. However, Anderson’s passing game shares traits with De Bruyne. In time, it will not be a surprise to see Anderson become a regular provider of assists for Manchester City. Also, Anderson has the potential to score goals from midfield. item.title: ‘Worst search of all time’ – Fans have their say after Russell Wilson interviews to be a CFB head coach
item.description: Photo by ANGELA WEISS / AFP via Getty Images Russell Wilson has emerged as a leading contender for a college football head coaching role despite never coaching football at any level. Wilson is a Super Bowl-winning QB who was one of his generation’s standout talents before a slow decline saw fans turn against him as he retired after the 2025 NFL season due to declining performances. While the 37-year-old has become a major media figure since retirement, it seems he could be headed to the NCAA after interviewing for the vacant head coaching role at his alma mater, NC State. Russell Wilson joining NC State HC search has fans upset Adam Schefter reported that Wilson, who played for NC State from 2008 to 2010, interviewed for the vacant head coaching role, joining another former NC State and NFL QB, Phillip Rivers, in the race. “Sources: former Super Bowl champion QB Russell Wilson interviewed today for the head coaching job at North Carolina State, where he played three seasons. NC State now has two former NFL greats who starred there, Wilson and Philip Rivers, as prominent head-coaching candidates.” Fans are not pleased with this, thinking that the college program is not treating their HC search seriously. “This has to be the worst job search of all time,” slammed a fan . “Man. Did not see that coming,” said one stunned fan . “It’s very possible an NC State message board is making all major decisions regarding their coaching hire,” said one fan, criticising the move . “Wilson vs. Rivers for the NC State job: one brings a Super Bowl ring, the other brings a minivan full of future recruits,” said another fan . “So they’re just trolling with that job, fairs,” said another fan negatively . NC State fired longtime head coach Dave Doeren after a 3-4 start to the season on October 24. He’s arguably the greatest coach in program history after a 14-year tenure, with this decision also meaning a complete revamp of their football program. Wilson was an accomplished three-year player with NC State but would transfer to Wisconsin for his final season after disagreements with the old coaching staff. Wilson has no formal coaching experience. His biggest rival for the job currently, Phillip Rivers, is at least an accomplished high school coach and has his son in the team’s QB pipeline. Rivers is also a former NC State QB and NFL star, and would make a challenging but natural jump to the NCAA after six years in high school. Wilson is a media figure now, so it’s understandable to see fans frustrated at NC State not looking at more traditional options to keep them competitive while giving them the structure they need to rebuild. Smith names the new favourites to win the Super Bowl ‘Finally said it on record’ – Dallas Cowboys insider stunned Jerry Jones finally confirmed his coach strategy Micah Parsons and Dan Orlovsky engage in brutal back-and-forth over ‘most clutch quarterback’ in NFL

item.title: Sanusi credits Tinubu for rescuing Nigeria’s economy from brink
item.description: The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, has said President Bola Tinubu deserves credit for bringing Nigeria’s economy back from the brink, citing improvements in economic growth, inflation, foreign reserves and export diversification. Sanusi, however, cautioned that significant economic challenges remain, saying the country must sustain its current growth trajectory to achieve lasting stability. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) spoke on Tuesday at the Oxford Global Think Tank conference convened by Arunma Oteh. “I’m not a fan of politicians, but we need to give credit to President Tinubu’s administration for bringing us back from the brink,” he said. Sanusi cited the country’s economic growth of 4.48 per cent in the second quarter of 2026, describing it as an improvement over the average performance recorded during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari. “GDP in Q2 2026 was at 4.48 percent. It’s not as high as it was under the Yar’Adua/Jonathan government, but during the Buhari years, the economy grew by 0.9 percent. Today it’s at 4.5 percent. That’s progress,” he said. He also highlighted the decline in inflation from about 30 per cent to 14.6 per cent, noting that it was projected to fall further to 12.5 per cent by the end of the year. On economic growth and living standards, the emir said Nigeria’s gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, measured in dollar terms, had increased by 47 per cent since 2023. He expressed optimism that sustaining the current pace of growth could restore the country’s GDP per capita to its 2005 level by the end of next year. “If we continue at this rate, by the end of next year, GDP per capita will be back to where it was in 2005,” he said. Sanusi also pointed to Nigeria’s foreign reserves, which he put at $55 billion, but warned that a substantial portion of the inflows was driven by foreign portfolio investments, which could be volatile. “Our reserves are at $55 billion, and yes, a lot of it is driven by portfolio flows, which are volatile,” he said. He attributed the continued inflows partly to high oil prices amid the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and attractive returns available to investors in Nigeria. On export diversification, Sanusi said 20 per cent of Nigeria’s exports were coming from the Dangote Refinery, describing the development as evidence of progress beyond the country’s traditional export sources. Despite acknowledging the economic gains, the former CBN governor criticised the Tinubu administration’s communication strategy, saying the government appeared to interpret criticism and constructive suggestions as attacks. “This government doesn’t express itself properly. It sees every suggestion and contribution it does not like as an attack, and it doesn’t have good spokespersons,” he said. item.title: Rohit Sharma’s record in Auckland: How Hitman has performed at Eden Park in all formats
item.description: Rohit Sharma’s record in Auckland: How Hitman has performed at Eden Park in all formats originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Rohit Sharma returns to Eden Park for India 's 1st ODI against New Zealand on November 4. He averages 49.00 in ODIs at the ground but has never passed 43 there in the format. His 72 in the 2014 Test remains his highest score at Eden Park in any format. Has Rohit Sharma played at Eden Park? Rohit Sharma has a longer history at Eden Park than at most overseas grounds, having played there in all three formats across a span of 17 years. What he does not have is a defining innings at the venue. He has appeared in three ODIs, three T20Is and one Test at the Auckland ground, the first of them in March 2009 and the most recent in January 2020. India have not played a Test there since 2014. Rohit trained at Eden Park on October 30 while the T20I squad was in Auckland, though he was not part of that leg, having retired from the format after the 2024 T20 World Cup. MORE: India and Pakistan could face each other upto 10 times in the upcoming year Rohit Sharma's record at Eden Park A format-by-format breakdown of his numbers at the ground. Format Matches Innings Runs Highest score Average Hundreds ODI 4 4 98 43* 24.50 0 T20I 3 3 65 50 21.66 0 Test 1 2 91 72 45.50 0 What is Rohit Sharma's record in ODIs at Eden Park, Auckland? Four innings have produced 98 runs at an average of 24.50 and a strike rate of 73.68, with four fours and five sixes. The average flatters the output, because two of the four innings ended with him not out or barely started. item.title: Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis
item.description: By Udeme Akpan Power sector experts have called for accelerated deployment of renewable energy and microgrids to address Nigeria’s persistent electricity supply challenges and reduce dependence on the national grid. Speaking in separate interviews with Vanguard at the recently concluded Nigeria Energy Summit in Lagos, they said decentralised power solutions would improve electricity access, particularly for businesses and rural communities. Product Manager, DEIF, Anshul Alankar, said: “The reality is that renewable energy is the in-thing, and government policy also supports it. It is important to latch on to it as early as possible, especially for the commercial sector and even for individual users. “The grid system is not able to provide all the electricity and power needed by Nigerians and Africans to maintain sustainable energy. “Nigeria has surplus solar energy, and microgrids will help because you don’t need huge infrastructure to bring power across the country. “Microgrids are a more efficient way of handling local and rural areas. You can create your own grid, minimise fuel consumption and maximise the sun, which is free.” On the growing demand for decentralised energy, he said: “We see that the need of the market is around microgrids and fuel efficiency. We provide solutions that enable batteries to work more efficiently and solar panels to be maximised.” Also speaking, Executive Director, Delmira Power Solutions, Dr. Moriam Jagun, said the company was bringing advanced power management solutions into Nigeria. She said its technologies “coordinate, protect and monitor energy, making sure that energy is efficiently generated and delivered, both for land and marine.” Sales Head, Engineering, Delmira Power Solutions, Engr. Nmecha Chizinum Ayodele, said: “Our country has come to the point of further expansion in renewable energy, from household to grid levels.” He added: “DEIF solutions can remotely monitor, automate and synchronise different power sources to provide all-round power for industries and homes, thereby reducing the cost of energy.” The post Experts push renewables to tackle Nigeria’s power crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Branford repeats as SCC field hockey champion on Savannah Johnson's double-OT goal
item.description: The Branford High field hockey team celebrates its second straight SCC title after defeating Hand 2-1 in double overtime Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, at Amity High in Woodbridge. (Kwame Colecraft/For Hearst Connecticut Media) WOODBRIDGE - The Branford field hockey team defeated Daniel Hand 2-1 in double overtime on Savannah Johnson's golden goal Tuesday night at William Johnson Stadium to win its second straight SCC championship. Johnson worked her way past two defenders and the goalkeeper before directing the ball into the net for the game-winner. Johnson's teammate Ellie Meyran was the first to give her a hug before the rest of the team and coaches joined the celebration. After playing defense for most of the game, Johnson and Meyran helped shift the momentum for Branford in overtime, creating chance after chance. "It was all excitement - I mean, [it was] stressful being in double overtime," Johnson said. "We've been in this situation before a few years ago for states, and unfortunately the result wasn't what we wanted two years ago, but now today, it was just awesome." Two years ago, Branford lost to Guilford 1-0 in the Class M final on a golden goal scored by Cassie Ward. Johnson said the result left a bitter taste for the Branford players who were there. Since then, the Hornets have never looked back, but head coach Pete Frye is also making sure his team does not look too far ahead. "Whoever the next team is, that's who we focus on, so hopefully we can play in three more," Frye said. The Hornets scored the first goal after a foul inside the shooting circle led to a penalty stroke, which captain Jessica Radziunas converted. "I always expect to make the [penalty] strokes," Radziunas said. "That's like a free shot for me, so getting an opportunity in the finals is amazing." Radziunas also led Branford's defense to a solid performance. After Radziunas' goal, Hand controlled possession for much of regulation, but Branford's defense held off its attacks until Campbell Leckey converted a penalty stroke to tie the game. Frye said that the defense was the key to victory in the game. Once overtime came, Branford turned the tables and attacked the Tigers' defense. "I couldn't be more proud of [my teammates]," Johnson said. "I love them so much, and I can't wait to see what happens during [the state tournament]." Branford is the defending Class M state champion and the No. 1 seed this year. After a first-round bye, the Hornets will host the winner of Nonnewaug-E.O. Smith in the quarterfinals. Hand is the No. 3 seed in M and will host No. 14 Lyman Hall in the first round. Player of the Game Savannah Johnson, Branford: Johnson scored the game-winning goal in overtime to give Branford consecutive SCC championships. item.title: SDSU offense explodes in season opener with six in double-figures to top Titans
item.description: San Diego State Aztecs guard Latrell Davis splits defenders during their game against the Cal State Fullerton Titans on November 3, 2026, at Viejas Arena in San Diego. SAN DIEGO – Behind a dominant effort from their starting five and a pair of 10-plus point runs in the second half, the San Diego State Aztecs pulled away with a 102-78 win over the Cal State Fullerton Titans on Tuesday night at Viejas Arena. Before the season head coach Brian Dutcher pointed to the play of his three starting guards as a key for the Aztecs’ aspirations. Against the Titans, the back court looked like the Godzilla monster King Gidorah, with each of the three heads helping to lay waste to the CSF defense. There was Latrell Davis, putting up 25 points in his SDSU regular season debut, the ninth time with 20-plus in his career, thanks to 5-of-7 shooting from 3. Elzie Harrington roared to life in the second half, scoring 9 of his 15 points after the break, and Chance Gladden dished out a game-high 8 assists, which equaled the third-most in a game in his career — the threesome combined for just 8 turnovers. It helped having powerful performances inside from forwards Bear Cherry and Tae Simmons. The fifth-year San Diego native scored 15 points with 7 rebounds and 4 blocks, while Simmons notched 14 points and 11 rebounds with 2 steals. Off the bench Luca Vincini chipped in 10 points and 7 boards. After scrapping their way to an 11-point lead at halftime, the bit of fortune from Harrington’s attempted alley-oop to Cherry going in early sparked the strongest Aztec run of the game. After a Josh Ward and-one for CSF, Harrington kicked off an 11-0 run by scoring 7 points in a row. Then back-to-back jams got the crowd roaring, as Simmons spun through the paint to throw it down and then on a fast break Davis lobbed it for Cherry to maul down and force a Titan timeout with a then game-high 19-point lead. Out of the breather Cal State Fullerton responded with a 10-0 run, taking advantage of a defense that gave too many easy paths to the basket respecting the Titans 3-point shooting. SAN DIEGO – Behind a dominant effort from their starting five and a pair of 10-plus point runs in the second half, the San Diego State Aztecs pulled away with a 102-78 win over the Cal State Fullerton Titans on Tuesday night at Viejas Arena. Elzie Harrington roared to life in the second half, scoring 9 of his 15 points after the break, and Chance Gladden dished out a game-high 8 assists, which equaled the third-most in a game in his career — the threesome combined for just 8 turnovers. It helped having powerful performances inside from forwards Bear Cherry and Tae Simmons. The fifth-year San Diego native scored 15 points with 7 rebounds and 4 blocks, while Simmons notched 14 points and 11 rebounds with 2 steals. Off the bench Luca Vincini chipped in 10 points and 7 boards. After scrapping their way to an 11-point lead at halftime, the bit of fortune from Harrington’s attempted alley-oop to Cherry going in early sparked the strongest Aztec run of the game. After a Josh Ward and-one for CSF, Harrington kicked off an 11-0 run by scoring 7 points in a row. Then back-to-back jams got the crowd roaring, as Simmons spun through the paint to throw it down and then on a fast break Davis lobbed it for Cherry to maul down and force a Titan timeout with a then game-high 19-point lead. Out of the breather Cal State Fullerton responded with a 10-0 run, taking advantage of a defense that gave too many easy paths to the basket respecting the Titans 3-point shooting. Though pulling back within single-digits twice, it served to be just a stay of the result, as SDSU ripped off another big run, dashing off a dozen. The inside-outside efforts of Davis and Isaiah Sy hitting from outside, with Simmons and a pair from Vincini in the paint pushed the lead out to 20. Sy finished with 12 points and made two triples and all six of his free throws. Much of the opening 20 minutes was played at a herky-jerky clip as SDSU was in the bonus 30 seconds before the midway mark. In the early stages it was the battling in the paint by Cherry that led to back-to-back buckets, including one on a nice baseline-reverse step-through. Then the Scarlet and Black served their first spot of 3 from Davis after the English-born guard scored his first two buckets on slashes through the lane. But Cal State Fullerton didn’t allow SDSU to build a lead of more than two possessions in the initial stages, battling back with a pair of 3’s and then taking advantage of Cherry heading to the bench by scoring their next four buckets on paint drives. A back-cut baseline dunk by Malcolm Bell gave the Titans their first lead. It was part of a 13-2 stretch by the visitors where Bell responded to a pair of Sy freebie makes with a triple, then Bailey Nunn knocked in another from beyond to make it 25-19 Titans at the 10:42 mark. From there the Aztecs driving game helped them get to the line for what eventually became 25 times in the opening 20 minutes, with SDSU sinking 23. After Vincini put the Aztecs back in front with an elbow jumper, Davis’s third of three first half 3-pointers pushed the lead to multiple possessions. But the game swung at the 3:47 mark as Luka Skorić drew a loose-ball foul battling for an offensive rebound, which set Titans head coach Dedrique Taylor off and led to him being whistled for a technical foul. After all four free-throws fell, Sy making the technicals, a weaving Davis drive and score pushed the lead out to 9, then with the final 5 points of the half SDSU held their largest lead of the game at 54-43 at the break. SDSU finished 27-of-32 from the free throw line and dominated the glass to a 44-26 edge, including 16-10 on offense. It’s the first time the Scarlet and Black had scored 100 points against a DI school in a non-overtime game since beating Texas Southern 103-64 in the second game of the 2018-19 season. The Aztecs will not leave San Diego County until taking part in the annual Players Era tournament hosted in Las Vegas, beginning on Nov. 24. Up next is the Bill Walton Classic against the Colorado Buffaloes, who were picked to finish 15th by the media in the 16-team Big 12 conference. Then a home game against Bethune Cookman on Nov. 11 at Viejas Arena, with the Compete 4 Cancer Classic against New Mexico State hosted at Frontwave Center in Oceanside, Calif., before rounding the stretch by hosting Texas Southern on Nov. 18. The inaugural Bill Walton Classic will tip off at 12:30 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 7 at Pechanga Arena. It’s the same venue — then the Sports Arena — as the last time SDSU and Colorado met, with the Aztecs coming away with a 78-72 win during the 1975-76 season. The game will be televised on USA Network, with a local radio broadcast on 760AM KGB.

item.title: ‘Here Is a Big One’ — Media Insider Predicts Joe Buck’s Next MNF Partner Amid ESPN Drama, Floats Surprise Landing Spot for Troy Aikman
item.description: ESPN's Joe Buck and Troy Aikman. We have a whole, entire, sizzling NFL season running, but the headlines have really been all about Joe Buck and Troy Aikman’s falling out in the ESPN booth. With tension between the two, and no new deal in place for Aikman, the storied Monday Night Football partnership may be on the brink. If Aikman moves on, ESPN will, of course, need someone new beside Buck, while the Dallas Cowboys legend will have to decide what comes next. The Athletic’s Andrew Marchand has a prediction for both, and his idea for Aikman involves a platform outside traditional television. Andrew Marchand Names Joe Buck’s Potential New MNF Partner During a live Q&A about his reporting on the Buck-Aikman dispute, Marchand outlined how he expects the broadcast changes to unfold. He sees former FOX analyst Greg Olsen joining Buck at ESPN, while YouTube could give Aikman a new opportunity to remain involved in NFL coverage. “At this moment, I’d predict [Greg] Olsen is at ESPN, while — here is a big one — YouTube picks up a game or two and Aikman is the analyst next year,” Marchand said . Olsen has emerged as a leading candidate after losing FOX’s top analyst role to Tom Brady in 2024. His current contract expires after the season, making a move to ESPN possible if Aikman vacates the chair. Peyton Manning is another name ESPN reportedly favors, but Marchand has indicated that a full-time traveling broadcast role may not appeal to him. Manning prefers the flexibility of producing the ManningCast from home. DIVE IN: PFN’s Free NFL HQ — Team and Player Stats, Info, and More The uncertainty began after reports indicated Buck signed a six-year, $108 million extension with ESPN without informing Aikman. Aikman, who is completing a five-year, $90 million contract, reportedly felt betrayed by his longtime partner. His representatives sought a new deal worth around $30 million annually, but ESPN paused negotiations. Their disagreement became public behind the scenes before the Oct. 12 broadcast at SoFi Stadium. Buck confronted Aikman over his lack of communication, while Aikman pointed to the undisclosed contract extension. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The two are expected to remain professional on air through Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027, but their 25-season partnership is widely expected to end afterward. Aikman has already acknowledged uncertainty about his television future, describing his chances of returning next season as “50-50.” Marchand’s YouTube prediction offers another route if the former quarterback does not return to a traditional network booth. YouTube already holds the rights to NFL Sunday Ticket, and Marchand believes the platform could pursue a small package of exclusive games. Aikman could then serve as its lead analyst, giving the platform an established NFL voice. A return to Dallas could also be an option for Aikman. item.title: Lakers face Luka Doncic ‘malpractice’ warning as trade likelihood reaches 65%
item.description: Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images The Los Angeles Lakers have been warned that failing to strengthen their roster around Luka Doncic would be a major mistake, with NBA insider Jovan Buha putting the chances of a trade at 65 per cent. The Lakers have made an impressive 6-2 start to the season, largely thanks to Doncic’s outstanding form. However, questions remain over their depth, particularly at centre and on the wing. With the Western Conference looking increasingly competitive, Los Angeles could look to make additions before the trade deadline to improve its championship chances. Jovan Buha says Los Angeles Lakers would be making a mistake by not trading Speaking on his podcast, Buha’s Block , the insider explained why the Lakers need to take advantage of Doncic’s current form rather than leave gaps in the roster. “If the Lakers don’t make a move and don’t try to improve this roster, it would be, to quote you, malpractice,” Buha said. “I just think that would be a giant mistake having Luka in his prime, potentially the best season of his career, and to not improve a couple of holes in the roster.” Buha believes Los Angeles has a strong opportunity to compete in the West and should be prepared to act. “Odds of making a trade, I would say like 65% right now,” he added. However, the insider does not necessarily expect the Lakers to make an immediate move. He suggested the franchise could wait until it has a clearer understanding of its rotation and where the biggest problems lie. “If someone goes down, maybe there’s a different need, or there’s some urgency to do something, or if they just continue to struggle to navigate some of these bench groups, maybe they feel some urgency to get a center at some point in December,” Buha said. The Lakers have reportedly been looking for another centre to provide cover behind Walker Kessler, while an upgrade at starting forward is also among their priorities. Doncic’s form makes the situation particularly important. He is averaging 38.3 points, 8.1 assists and eight rebounds per game, putting himself firmly in the MVP conversation. There is also a longer-term consideration. Doncic’s current contract could run through 2028 or 2029, depending on his player option, and ESPN’s Brian Windhorst has previously highlighted the importance of keeping the Lakers in a strong position to secure an extension. For Rob Pelinka and the front office, the challenge is finding the right additions without rushing into a deal. But Buha’s warning makes one thing clear: the Lakers cannot afford to waste Doncic’s current form. item.title: US Midterm: Democrats Retake Senate In Major Blow Against Trump’s Republicans
item.description: Democrats won full control of the US Congress in a sweeping midterm rout Tuesday with a landslide of upsets that delivered a crushing rebuke of President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.” But minutes later on social media, the 80-year-old signaled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.” The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of the party’s inroads into Republican strongholds. The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters. Texas was a political bombshell. Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office. Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority. The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved. Supporters of Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico cheer after he won the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Republican Heartland Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina. Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries. One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. The victory handed Democrats both the House of Representatives and Senate, giving them power to block Trump’s agenda and investigate alleged corruption for the last two years of his presidency. The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president. Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats.” But minutes later on social media, the 80-year-old signaled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.” The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night. In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932. Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of the party’s inroads into Republican strongholds. The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters. Texas was a political bombshell. Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office. Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire. Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority. The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved. Supporters of Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico cheer after he won the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Republican Heartland Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina. Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries. One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. Analysts had identified an upset there as a warning of a much wider Democratic advance. In Georgia, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor in US history, while other Democratic gains extended to statehouses across the country. Republicans had some bright spots in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds won the governorship, becoming the state’s first Black governor, and Ashley Moody kept a Senate seat. George Washington University professor Todd Belt called the Democratic advance “a big wipeout and a strong repudiation of Donald Trump and his policies,” citing voters’ concerns about the economy, corruption and the Iran conflict. Democratic US Senate candidate James Talarico celebrates with supporters after winning the Texas race during a midterm election night watch party at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on November 3, 2026. Trump On Defensive Democrats will now be able to block Trump’s legislation, investigate his administration over corruption allegations, the Iran war and immigration enforcement, and use Senate control to thwart judicial appointments and senior nominations. Robert Garcia, a Democrat expected to lead the powerful House Oversight Committee, warned Republicans on social media: “LAWYER UP.” House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries declared Trump’s MAGA movement “on the run from sea to shining sea.” Jeffries is also positioned to become the first Black speaker of the House when the new Congress convenes in January, if elected by his colleagues. For many voters, the central concern was Trump’s stewardship of the economy. “Rent, groceries, utility bills, and property taxes keep climbing,” 24-year-old Los Angeles voter Taylor Cook told AFP. item.title: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness — Feese
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit on Tuesday in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Power, logistics and so on and so forth.” She added that Nigeria needed to move beyond its domestic market and develop the capacity to supply other African countries. Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. The post Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness — Feese appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC vows to proceed with Sokoto campaign despite intimidation
item.description: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has vowed to proceed with its scheduled campaign in Sokoto State despite what it described as attempts by the state government to intimidate the opposition and obstruct its political activities. The party also warned that Governor Ahmed Aliyu would be held responsible if any violence was directed at opposition members or supporters in the state. The ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, stated this in a statement issued on Tuesday, accusing the Sokoto State Government of undermining democratic rights and deliberately frustrating the party’s activities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Abdullahi said the party would not be deterred by the alleged intimidation, insisting that no governor had the authority to prevent any political party from campaigning or presenting its candidates to voters. “The Sokoto State Government must understand that governing a state does not confer ownership. Public office is a temporary mandate from the people, not a licence to suppress political competition,” the statement read. “No governor has the power to decide which party can campaign, which candidate can speak, or which political choices the people of Sokoto are allowed to consider.” The ADC spokesperson called on the state government to immediately stop what he described as efforts to frustrate its lawful political activities and guarantee a level playing field for all political parties. He also reminded security agencies and other public institutions that their responsibility was to the Constitution and the Nigerian people, rather than the political interests of the ruling party. Abdullahi warned that public officials who abused their authority to obstruct lawful political activities would face the legal consequences of their actions. “Let there be no misunderstanding. The ADC will campaign in Sokoto State. We will not be intimidated, obstructed or pushed out of any part of Nigeria simply because those in power are afraid of political competition,” he said. He maintained that democratic participation was a constitutional right and not a privilege to be granted by elected public officials. The ADC spokesperson further accused the ruling party of displaying intolerance towards opposition activities, challenging it to submit itself to an open contest if it believed it had performed well in government. item.title: College Football Playoff committee completely screwed up initial CFP rankings reveal
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images. College Football Playoff committee completely screwed up initial CFP rankings reveal appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The first College Football Playoff rankings should clarify how the committee separates contenders. Tuesday’s reveal instead created three difficult questions about the value of winning, head-to-head results and the distance between otherwise competitive teams. Alabama at No. 5, UCLA at No. 8 and Ohio State at No. 12 form the clearest case against the initial order. Each placement has a defense. Together, they make the committee’s priorities difficult to follow. Alabama’s advantage over Tennessee is excessive The Alabama Crimson Tide and Tennessee Volunteers both hold 6-2 records, yet the committee ranked Alabama eight spots above the team that defeated it 26-10 on October 17. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Tennessee held the Crimson Tide to 201 yards and forced four turnovers. That performance deserves substantial weight when comparing teams with identical overall records. Alabama has an answer. Its victories over No. 6 Kentucky and No. 21 South Carolina strengthen its profile. Tennessee lost to South Carolina and No. 7 Texas, giving the committee legitimate reasons to distinguish their overall schedules. Those differences explain a debate. They do not convincingly explain eight positions. Tennessee should be much closer to Alabama , particularly when its strongest victory came directly against the team receiving a potential home playoff game. UCLA deserves more credit for remaining unbeaten The UCLA Bruins are 8-0, but five teams with losses separate them from unbeaten, top-ranked Miami. Two of those teams, Alabama and Texas, have lost twice. An undefeated record does not automatically establish a superior resume. Opponent quality matters, and UCLA’s schedule warrants scrutiny. Still, the Bruins won 17-15 at Oregon , which the committee ranked No. 23. They have both a perfect record and a road victory against a currently ranked opponent. That combination deserves more credit than eighth. The committee can reward difficult schedules without making an unbeaten Power conference team’s successful results feel secondary to opportunities other teams failed to convert. Ohio State’s win over Indiana deserves greater weight The Indiana Hoosiers are 8-1 and fourth. The Ohio State Buckeyes are 6-2 and 12th, despite winning 19-15 in Bloomington on October 17. Ohio State’s subsequent 30-18 loss at USC matters . So does quarterback Julian Sayin’s unavailability. The committee can consider injuries and evaluate the entire season. But Indiana’s only defeat came at home against Ohio State. That direct comparison should keep the teams closer, even if the Hoosiers retain the higher ranking. item.title: “He Chickened Out” – Carlos Prates Mocks Islam Makhachev’s Active Champion Promise After UFC 336 Snub
item.description: Carlos Prates after knocking out Leon Edwards at UFC 322 | Photo: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kshitiz Kumar Singh Islam Makhachev’s decision to pull out of negotiations for UFC 336 has sparked plenty of controversy. The Dagestani was slated to defend his welterweight title against Carlos Prates on the January 30 card in Toronto. However, Makhachev backed out, arguing that there were too many contenders in the division and that Prates and Michael Morales should settle the No. 1 contender debate themselves. His decision drew criticism from both the Brazilian and UFC CEO Dana White. Now, Prates and Morales are set to clash for the interim welterweight title in the Great White North. Since the announcement, Prates has continued to take shots at Makhachev. The Brazilian recently warned that he would ruin the Dagestani’s legacy when they eventually meet. A heated exchange with Makhachev’s manager, Ali Abdelaziz, also lit up social media, and Prates clearly has no intention of holding back. Carlos Prates Promises to Make Islam Makhachev Pay After Beating Michael Morales In a recent interview with Laerte Viana , Prates accused Makhachev of backing out of their planned UFC 336 title fight. He said, “He comes out saying he wants to be an active champion, this and that. Hunter [Campbell] even said that date was reserved for him. Then he just came out and said he didn’t want it. He chickened out.” Although Prates is understandably frustrated with how things played out, he knows he first needs to get past Morales and claim the interim title. Once that’s out of the way, he plans to turn his attention back to Makhachev. He said, “I was pretty pissed off, but what can you do? The situation I’m in now is that I have to beat Morales and win the interim belt. I’m going to focus on him, then I’m going to come back and beat Makhachev twice as hard just to teach him a lesson.” Prates also stressed that Makhachev’s decision has delayed a dream he has spent 17 years chasing. The Brazilian is clearly determined to make the Dagestani pay when they finally share the Octagon. He concluded with, “I’ve been in this game for 17 years, and when it finally came time for me to fulfill my dream of becoming a champion, this dude pulls some bullsh*t like that. I was really pissed off. item.title: Petrol hits N1,370/litre as depot prices rise
item.description: By Udeme Akpan The pump price of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, has risen to N1,370 per litre in Lagos, following fresh increases in depot prices across major supply locations. Checks by Vanguard on Tuesday showed that MRS and NNPC filling stations sold petrol at N1,360 per litre, while Mobil sold at N1,349. Some independent marketers sold at between N1,365 and N1,370, depending on location. The increase followed sharp movements in depot prices, particularly in Lagos, where A.A. Rano raised its PMS price by N75 to N1,295 per litre, while African Terminal, Aiteo and Integrated increased their prices to about N1,300. NIPCO also raised its price by N55 to N1,305, while Dangote’s price edged up by N3 to N1,303. MRS retained its depot price at N1,310. In Port Harcourt, Matrix increased its PMS price by N15 to N1,300 per litre, while Bulk Strategic, Masters and T.S.L remained at N1,300. Warri also recorded increases, with A.Y.M. Shafa and Matrix raising their prices by N17 each to N1,300, while Parker moved up by N15 to the same level. Calabar recorded higher PMS prices, with Fynefield and Northwest at N1,360 per litre. Meanwhile, Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), or diesel, recorded mixed movements. In Lagos, WOSBAB cut its AGO price by N21 to N1,809 per litre, while Bulk Strategic reduced its price by N15 to N1,835. Rain Oil and Dangote also reduced their prices to N1,850 and N1,823 respectively. In Warri, Matrix and Rain Oil cut their AGO prices by N5 each to N1,835 per litre, while Edo Refinery, NIPCO and Prudent retained theirs at N1,840. The latest figures point to continued volatility in the downstream market as changes in depot prices filter through to retail outlets. “To safeguard port integrity and vessel safety, all maritime operators, terminal users, and personnel must utilise authorised reporting protocols immediately upon detecting any security incident or anomaly,” the agency stated. The post Petrol hits N1,370/litre as depot prices rise appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Pat Surtain II Reacts to Jaylen Waddle’s Post After Broncos Beat Chiefs
item.description: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos reacts during the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) Getty Jaylen Waddle had a touchdown, a two-point conversion and a four-word reply from Pat Surtain II after the Denver Broncos beat the Kansas City Chiefs to take over first place in the AFC West. Waddle posted an Instagram carousel that opened with a photo of him in his white No. 17 Broncos jersey. His caption read, “REORGANIZE MY WHOLE GANG…” Surtain chimed in with “Wake em up !” Linebacker Alex Singleton also replied with an emoji. Two days earlier, the question was whether Waddle would play at all. The Broncos had listed him as questionable with a chest injury. He played, and Bo Nix went to him twice with points on the line in a 28-24 win. View this post on Instagram Jaylen Waddle Delivered Twice Near the Goal Line Against Kansas City Waddle finished with three catches for 39 yards and a touchdown, according to Denver’s official game log. His longest catch went for 35 yards. His shortest came from a yard out, when Nix found him on fourth down for Denver’s first touchdown. Waddle’s other scoring catch came in the fourth quarter, after Nix hit tight end Nate Adkins for a touchdown on another fourth down. Denver had trailed 24-13. Waddle caught the two-point try to make it 24-21, giving the Broncos a chance to tie with a field goal on their next scoring possession. They wound up getting seven instead. Rookie running back Jonah Coleman set up his own go-ahead touchdown with a 51-yard catch and run. Kansas City still drove to the Denver 1-yard line, but a false start pushed the Chiefs back on fourth down and Malcolm Roach sacked Patrick Mahomes to finish the game, according to the Broncos’ game recap . Denver Got More From Waddle in the Chiefs Rematch When the teams met in Week 1, Waddle caught one pass for 2 yards in a 31-10 loss. His second game against Kansas City showed two ways Denver can use him in the same afternoon. He supplied a 35-yard gain, then gave Nix a target in tight quarters on a fourth down and a conversion attempt. It was Waddle’s second touchdown of the season. He has 29 catches for 315 yards through eight games, with 138 of those yards coming against Jacksonville in Week 2. He has yet to reach 50 yards in any of his other seven games. The Chiefs rematch showed how he can still swing a close game on three catches. Denver has won four straight to get to 6-2 and heads to Carolina on Sunday, Nov. 8, before its bye week . Against Kansas City, Waddle entered the weekend as a game-day question and ended it as the receiver Nix trusted twice near the goal line. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Pat Surtain II Reacts to Jaylen Waddle’s Post After Broncos Beat Chiefs appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘This Would Literally Ruin Basketball,’ ‘Do Not Do That’ — NBA World Outraged As Adam Silver ‘Likes the Idea’ Of 40-Minute Games
item.description: 'This Would Literally Ruin Basketball,' 'Do Not Do That' -- NBA World Outraged As Adam Silver 'Likes the Idea' Of 40-Minute Games NBA fans are pushing back against the possibility of shorter games after a recent report suggested Adam Silver prefers reducing NBA contests from 48 to 40 minutes. Sports Illustrated’s Chris Mannix recently discussed the commissioner’s preference, but the idea is not new, and Silver has openly supported it before. NBA Fans Outraged as Adam Silver’s 40-Minute Game Preference Resurfaces Mannix discussed the possibility during a recent appearance alongside Rachel Nichols on Sports Illustrated. He said Silver likes the idea of replacing the NBA’s traditional four 12-minute quarters with four 10-minute periods, bringing games in line with the international format. “Adam Silver likes the idea of 40-minute games. Adam’s a globalist when it comes to basketball. But I just don’t see financially how it is feasible,” Mannix said . He also explained that shortening games would not necessarily reduce the workload of the biggest stars. Instead, he believes players further down the rotation would lose opportunities. The comments quickly drew criticism from basketball fans, many of whom believe changing the length of NBA games would affect the sport’s identity and history. “This would literally ruin basketball,” one hoops fan wrote . A Pacers fan account also warned about the impact on historical comparisons, saying : “NO… this would change basketball history and how we compare stats across generations.” Others directed their frustration at the commissioner, as one user wrote : “Adam Silver needs to be fired IMMEDIATELY.” “This dude sucks at his job,” a sports content creator quipped. “Do not do that lol,” a user posted. However, the first time Silver publicly expressed the idea was in January 2025. He appeared on The Dan Patrick Show and openly said he was a fan of four 10-minute quarters. “As we get more involved in global basketball, the NBA is the only league that plays 48 minutes,” Silver explained . “I am a fan of four 10-minute quarters.” Silver argued that a two-hour game would better fit modern television viewing habits, citing Olympic and college basketball, both of which use a 40-minute format. He also acknowledged that shortening games could affect records and statistics, although he said he was putting those concerns aside when discussing the idea. At the time, ESPN reported that NBA games averaged 2 hours and 16 minutes, making them considerably longer than the two-hour format Silver preferred. The discussion also drew opposition from coaches.
