MORE: ‘No Kidding,’ ‘Who Wants to Be In Sacramento?’ — NBA Insider Gets Brutally Honest on Rumor That Domantas Sabonis Wants Kings to Trade Him A switch would have significant consequences beyond the length of games. NBA games have featured four 12-minute quarters throughout the league’s history, and reducing them to 10 minutes would make many scoring and playing-time records harder to compare across generations. While Mannix’s latest comments have revived an old debate, they do not mean the league is preparing to introduce 40-minute games. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Brian Brobbey’s Here To Stay: Our Writers React
item.description: MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Brian Brobbey of Sunderland scores his team's first goal during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester City and Sunderland at Etihad Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Matt McNulty/Getty Images) | Getty Images Alex Charlton says… I have to say this caught me by surprise, especially given the state of our season. On the face of it, this is obviously fantastic news. Brobbey has been one of our best signings of the Premier League era, scoring big goals in big matches. Given he doesn’t score a lot of goals, I feel he doesn’t always get the credit he deserves. He offers so much with his hold-up play and strength and is so much more than just a striker. Let’s hope he plays a significant role in keeping us in the league and progressing in Europe. However, if we were to get relegated, I can’t see Brobbey staying. Yes, this contract ties him down for five years but I would expect him to leave for a sizable fee next summer if things don’t go to plan. Let’s hope he’s focused on the job at hand and can fire us up the table. All in all, it’s great business and the positive news we need in a difficult time. Ian Clark says… Panic over — I thought he was injured or had asked to leave! Great news. It shows he’s happy and wants to stay. A deserved reward financially for him and it us some security too that a would-be buying club will need to pay top dollar for him. If he become more clinical — for example, taking chances like the one he skewed wide against Coventry — he could be worth £100+ million, given all his other qualities. It looks like a deal where club and player both win — now let’s see him get back to terrorising Premier League defences and scoring regularly. John Wade says… Superb news. Brobbey is so very important to us when holding the ball up and usually occupying at least two defenders. It’s up to us to get the best out of that — something we aren’t necessarily doing at the moment. Could he be more clinical? Yes. He’s missed a few chances a lesser striker would be disappointed with. Will it come? I hope so. Either way, this suggests he’s happy at the club — something I’m sure even he thought might not happen when he arrived so unhappy and out of sorts generally. The issues he had in his private life in Holland are surely behind him now and I see nothing but improvement from him going forward. And if he does ever want to go, think of all that lovely money we’ll get. Malc Dugdale says… This is a great piece of news for fans and for the club alike and to get this across the line right now is a welcome injection of positivity too. When clubs start to struggle a bit, key players can get jittery and vultures from so-called bigger clubs can circle more intensely. Convincing Brobbey this is the place to be for the next five years is no mean feat given the dilemma we find in ourselves right now. (Photo by Matt McNulty/Getty Images) | Getty Images Alex Charlton says… I have to say this caught me by surprise, especially given the state of our season. On the face of it, this is obviously fantastic news. Brobbey has been one of our best signings of the Premier League era, scoring big goals in big matches. Yes, this contract ties him down for five years but I would expect him to leave for a sizable fee next summer if things don’t go to plan. Let’s hope he’s focused on the job at hand and can fire us up the table. All in all, it’s great business and the positive news we need in a difficult time. Ian Clark says… Panic over — I thought he was injured or had asked to leave! Great news. It shows he’s happy and wants to stay. A deserved reward financially for him and it us some security too that a would-be buying club will need to pay top dollar for him. If he become more clinical — for example, taking chances like the one he skewed wide against Coventry — he could be worth £100+ million, given all his other qualities. It looks like a deal where club and player both win — now let’s see him get back to terrorising Premier League defences and scoring regularly. John Wade says… Superb news. Brobbey is so very important to us when holding the ball up and usually occupying at least two defenders. It’s up to us to get the best out of that — something we aren’t necessarily doing at the moment. Could he be more clinical? Yes. He’s missed a few chances a lesser striker would be disappointed with. The issues he had in his private life in Holland are surely behind him now and I see nothing but improvement from him going forward. And if he does ever want to go, think of all that lovely money we’ll get. Malc Dugdale says… This is a great piece of news for fans and for the club alike and to get this across the line right now is a welcome injection of positivity too. When clubs start to struggle a bit, key players can get jittery and vultures from so-called bigger clubs can circle more intensely. Convincing Brobbey this is the place to be for the next five years is no mean feat given the dilemma we find in ourselves right now. He’s had periods of injury and that’s probably been part of the reason for his conversion of chances being less clinical than last season. I’m sure that sharpness will increase with time, and even if he just sucks in two or three players for the rest of the season, this will massively help us to succeed with those around him grabbing goals and valuable points. Well done to the club hierarchy for what’s as a minimum a huge insurance policy on a player that could be worth well north of £50 million already, and more if this season works out well for him and for us all.

item.title: OTD (4/11/1972): Billy Elliott’s Sunderland Debut Brings Fireworks
item.description: Billy Elliott, Sunderland (Photo by Barratts/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images Alan Brown was not the first manager I experienced at Roker Park, but he was the manager I grew up with. His departure was something of a shock to me as a young fan. I had assumed that, like my parents, he would always be there! item.content:encoded: Billy Elliott, Sunderland (Photo by Barratts/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images Alan Brown was not the first manager I experienced at Roker Park, but he was the manager I grew up with. His departure was something of a shock to me as a young fan. I had assumed that, like my parents, he would always be there! Billy Elliott had been shown the door at Roker Park as a player by Alan Brown in 1957. He had then been invited back as a coach in 1968. One of Elliott’s first jobs was coaching the youth team and, in 1969, he coached that team to the FA Youth Cup final and victory. Fourteen games into the 1972/73 season, with the club in 14th position in the table and gates dipping below 12,000, Brown resigned and Billy Elliott was installed as caretaker manager whilst the board figured out if they could get Clough or Revie (the fans’ choice) in as Brown’s replacement. Aston Villa at Roker Park was to be Elliott’s first game in temporary control. Typical of the blunt-speaking Yorkshireman that he was, he told Ken Gorman of The Journal: “I am no stuffed dummy, I wouldn’t worry about having to speak my mind to anyone, including our directors.” Elliott was 47 years old at the time. He had gained five England caps as a player at Bradford, Burnley and Sunderland, before finishing off at non-league Wisbech Town, having been released by Brown. Hanging up his boots, Elliott had gone on to coach the Libyan national team, USA servicemen in Germany and manage Belgian club Royal Daring, before coming back to Roker Park as part of Brown’s coaching team. For his first game in temporary control, he wasted no time in making some tough decisions. He dropped Joe Bolton and John Lathan and relegated Mick McGiven to the subs’ bench, bringing in transfer-listed Keith Coleman and Brian Chambers, as well as Billy Hughes, who had just come off the transfer list. He moved Bobby Kerr back to the right-hand side of midfield and opted for a very attacking line-up to try and end a run of one point from four games. Aston Villa, like Sunderland, were something of a sleeping giant. Managed by the experienced Vic Crowe, they were pushing hard for promotion and were well in touch at this point in the season. Even though the dangerous forward Andy Lochhead was not available, Villa had a strong squad that included some players who would go on to have fine careers. The likes of Chris Nicholl, John Gidman, Alun Evans, Brian Little and Bruce Rioch were players who would grace the game for a generation. Sunderland’s biggest gate of the season, 7,000 up on the last home game, turned up to see if the team could react to Alan Brown’s departure – and what a spirited, all-action performance they saw. I had just made it to my left-of-centre position in the Fulwell End when Villa captain Bruce Rioch attempted a long diagonal pass back to his keeper. The ball fell invitingly for the returning Billy Hughes, who strode majestically forward, rounded Cumbes in the Villa goal and nonchalantly put the ball in the back of the net. What a start to the game and what a roar it got from the crowd. Hughesie had a characteristic way of marking his goals, and I can picture him still, arms aloft, strutting like a peacock and milking the applause. He knew how to celebrate a goal and work the crowd, did Billy! The goal was the signal for Sunderland to pour forward at every opportunity, and for 20 minutes Villa could hardly get a touch as Ian Porterfield stroked the ball all over the park to ready and willing team-mates eager to add to the lead they had taken. Cumbes more than earned his match bonus in this period alone, as he just about kept Villa in the game. It was typical of the way things had gone for us in this season so far that the first error made led to a Villa equaliser. Keith Coleman had enjoyed a great opening period to the game, with a couple of good runs, solid tackles and interventions, as well as some clever use of the ball. Despite being a big Joe Bolton fan, I always thought Coleman worked in well with Ian Porterfield on that left-hand side. One area of his game that needed work, in my opinion (as a young teenage expert!), was his tendency towards an impetuous challenge. He went for a tackle he had no right to go for against Bruce Rioch, who slipped the challenge and, in the space he had created, slammed a cracking shot from the edge of the box that went in off the foot of the post. It was a good goal by Rioch, who probably felt he needed to atone for his opening-minute error. Rioch then took the game by the scruff of its neck and had two blockbuster attempts that caused a bit of frantic defending. His first shot had Jimmy Montgomery scuttling across his goal as the ball flew just past the post. Then another shot, which was goalbound, cannoned off a defender and fell to Evans in the box. His attempt was cleared brilliantly off the line by Dick Malone. Back came Sunderland through Dennis Tueart. A drive down the right wing led to a powerful shot that Cumbes saved, diving full-length. Moments later, Tueart came down the left wing and cannoned a shot that had the Fulwell End surging in anticipation of the net rippling. The ball sped just past the post. Half-time saw the Lads warmly applauded from the pitch. It had been a pulsating 45 minutes. The second half resumed in the same fashion as the first, with both teams looking for the next goal. It was a sharp contrast to some of the games in the latter days of Alan Brown’s reign, where low-risk, careful football appeared to be what the Sunderland team had been instructed to deliver. Evans beat Richie Pitt all ends up with a mazy run and short pass to Peterlee-born Brian Little, whose attempt produced a marvellous point-blank save from Monty. Rioch was influencing the game in every way possible, as he brought down Tueart right on the byline just after the hour. Ian Porterfield stepped up to take the kick and, with a clever feint, caressed a ball into the near post when it looked like he was going longer. The ball looked, in that split-second, as if it was going to nobody in particular, when a galloping Bobby Kerr arrived and got an angled touch with his head that deflected the ball at pace, across the keeper and in at the far post. If that was a rehearsed move, it was a cracker. The ground erupted as Bobby blessed us with his trademark forward-roll celebration. Villa were no soft touch at this time and came back strongly. Just six minutes after conceding, they were back level. I remember this as a bit of a soft goal. An aimless cross looped into the box that should have been dealt with (highlighting a difficulty in the air defensively). Brian Little, possibly the second smallest player on the pitch behind Bobby Kerr, rose to get a scruffy touch on the ball. Montgomery might have done better with this one, but it seemed as if the awkward contact created a moment of indecision and the ball looped limply over his head and crept into the net at the angle of the bar and post. It was a bit of a sickener, but back came Sunderland, with Porterfield finding a great pass to Watson (who had been engaged in a cracking contest with Villa centre-half Chris Nicholl for most of the game). His attempt was only an inch or two past the post. What then ensued was a ding-dong battle as both teams went for the winner. Sunderland probably came the closest to finding this in the very last minute of the game, when Tueart had another rousing run and rasping shot that was saved by Cumbes at his near post. On reflection, a draw was probably a fair result. Porterfield was player of the match for me, but honourable mentions go to Tueart and Kerr. The three lads returning to the team gave Elliott something to ponder for the next game, with Chambers showing some nice touches in midfield. Villa manager Vic Crowe was satisfied with the result that kept his team in the promotion race. He told reporters: “It was a hard match played at a terrific pace.

item.title: Fiery Fermín López leads the hunt as Barcelona overwhelm Aston Villa
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 03: Fermin Lopez of FC Barcelona interacts with teammate Joao Cancelo during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between FC Barcelona and Aston Villa FC at Camp Nou on November 03, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by David Ramos - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images Barcelona need Fermín López more than they probably realize. When things don’t go their way in the biggest games, it’s often because there is a drop in intensity that their opponents take advantage of. Fermín has become the warrior of the Camp Nou. For a stadium that has struggled to be the fortress that Barcelona needs it to be (I can tell you all about the 250 euro ticket prices to see Barca play Getafe that I did not pay), it helps to have a player who gets the fans, socios and tourists alike, out of their seats. It’s not just the moves of Lamine Yamal or the goals of Raphinha that get the stands rocking. It can also be the simple act of a player going the extra mile. Energy is contagious. At his best, Fermín is the guy with a chip on his shoulder. He’s in the starting lineup, and he knows he has to perform to keep himself there. He also understands the assignment that Hansi Flick has given the team. The front four must press intensely as a unit. Against Aston Villa , the fruits of this system, when the players are fully committed, were on display. For all the goals that Barcelona has scored, you get the sense that the chemistry between the forwards still isn’t fully clicking in the attack. Defensively, however, Flick has in place the exact characters that he needs. Anthony Gordon, Raphinha, and Fermín López are Flick’s type of guys. He can sleep well the night before a game knowing they will execute to the best of their ability on the gameplan. With the makeshift defense still in place, it’s even more important for the forwards to press effectively. Flick will have his players rewatch the tape against Aston Villa and say, here you go, this is how my system is supposed to look. It helps that Lamine was clinical with the chance that was created early on from the press. It can be hard after all to sustain such high intensity for a full 90 minutes. The backline still does look vulnerable. This game was the first clean sheet in Europe in the last 18 games. That stat tells the story of Barca’s Champions League disapointments. Aston Villa had their chances, but didn’t have on their finishing boots. Next up is a trip to Atletico Madrid who will be coming off a 2-0 loss to Bayern Munich at home. If the Bavarians can do it, so should Barcelona. The defenders will be tested again, and most likely, we’ll see the same guys, give or take Gerard Martín or Frenkie de Jong. Before the cavalry returns, the attacking players must step up again with the same defensive intensity and quality in front of goal. A win against Atleti would win back the goodwill of Barcelona’s fanbase, at least for the time being. It won’t come easy though. Ha

Hansi Flick is due to get payback against Diego Simeone, but he’ll have to get his lineup and tactics right. One player who looks ready and not afraid of the fight is Fermín López. Barcelona must prove that they’ve learned the harsh lesson that Atleti inflicted on them last season. This is an important chance at redemption, and a chance to show they’ve truly turned a page.

item.title: Rayan Ait-Nouri: Man United receive positive update in January pursuit of Man City ace
item.description: Rayan Ait-Nouri: Man United receive positive update in January pursuit of Man City ace Manchester United secured a stunning 3-2 comeback win over AS Roma at Old Trafford in the Champions League. However, the game further highlighted a gap in the squad that has been hurting the Red Devils for some time. Diogo Dalot started at left-back in the absence of Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu, both of whom are sidelined with injuries. The Portuguese defender has covered in the position before but is not a natural solution for the role. Dalot was caught out of position for Roma’s first goal, with Matias Soule afforded time and space to send the visitors ahead. While that ultimately amounted to nothing thanks to a Bruno Fernandes penalty and a late Matheus Cunha brace, United will look to address the issue in January. United failed to sign a left-back in the summer The Red Devils wanted to sign a new left-back this summer and among the candidates on their wish list was Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri. While INEOS failed to get a deal across the line, recent reports suggest that they are ready to return for the Algerian at the turn of the year. Ait-Nouri was a revelation for Wolverhampton Wanderers and moved to the Etihad in the summer of 2025. Unfortunately, he has struggled for game time with the Cityzens so far, and he could be tempted to leave in search of greener pastures in January. The 25-year-old has pace to burn, is attack-minded and knows the Premier League well. With also a point to prove after dropping down the pecking order at City, a move to Old Trafford could help him get his career back on track. A fresh update on the saga has now emerged, which could be music to the ears of the Red Devils faithful. R. Aït-Nouri Page 1 of 4 1 2 3 4 Personal terms not an issue for United move Journalist Florian Plettenberg has confirmed United’s interest in Ait-Nouri and insists that personal terms will not be a hindrance to the move. In a post shared on X, he wrote: “Rayan Aït-Nouri, one to watch in the winter transfer window.” “The 25 y/o left-back is open to leaving Manchester City. Understand Manchester United would like to sign him. Personal terms are not an issue.” However, Plettenberg warned that the Red Devils could struggle to convince their bitter rivals to let him go. He concluded: “The main issue is the relationship between the two Manchester clubs. Aït-Nouri’s market is currently being explored.” United and City have endured contrasting fortunes in the past decade, but their rivalry remains as intense as ever. The Cityzens may not be too keen to strengthen their archenemies, especially in the middle of the season. If the Red Devils find little luck in this pursuit, they could turn their attentions to Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, who is reportedly ready to leave Camp Nou in January. Recent reports suggest they also have their eyes on rising Rennes star Mahamadou Nagida. Why? ✅ United are reportedly eyeing a January move for Ait-Nouri. ✅ The Algerian

item.title: Brian Brobbey 2031 — A New Chapter In Red And White
item.description: As Sunderland fans, there’s little better than watching someone grow into the shirt. Brian Brobbey has already given us plenty to celebrate in his near-fifteen months on Wearside, and there are plenty of reasons to believe his story his just beginning. Tuesday’s announcement that our number nine has signed a new long-term contract, keeping him at the club until 2031, is a huge statement. Brobbey has become crucial to how Sunderland play, and this news, despite coming with the club at a low point, could act as both a catalyst to boost the fanbase and to inspire Brobbey to find his best form. Since arriving from Ajax on deadline day in 2025, Brobbey has brought a physical presence that many defenders have struggled to deal with, dominating Gabriel, William Saliba, Ruben Dias and of course Dan Burn during his time on Wearside. His first season saw him score seven Premier League goals as Sunderland exceeded expectations, securing Europa League football and announcing ourselves back in the Premier League — and there were plenty of memorable moments along the way. The winner at St James’ Park won’t be forgotten in a hurry, while his goals against Arsenal, Tottenham, Everton, Crystal Palace, Bournemouth and that assist at Stamford Bridge helped turn Sunderland’s Premier League return into something unheard of in these parts. If there was one afternoon that truly showed Brobbey’s potential, it was that hat-trick against Manchester City at the Etihad in September, with three goals against one of the strongest defences in the world, never mind the country. Each goal demonstrated a poacher’s instinct — similarly to his goals for Netherlands in the World Cup, both of which came from low crosses across the six-yard box. If we can keep creating these types of chances, Brobbey will continue to score and lead us to more positive results in the Premier League and on the continent this season. The Dutchman became the first Sunderland player to score a Premier League hat-trick since Jermain Defoe in 2016, and he also won the Premier League’s Player of the Matchweek award for his performance. This was a reminder that when it clicks and we create the chances, Brobbey can trouble any defence in the division. For Sunderland, this deal protects a key asset, increasing our bargaining power if a team were to come in for Brobbey in the next few transfer windows, as well as maximising our income in a worst-case scenario come the end of the season, but we won’t mention the ‘R’ word today. Brobbey also represents the type of player Sunderland are looking for and want to build around: ambitious, committed, physical and still developing. The first chapter has been a good one; let’s hope the next can be even better. To describe Brobbey’s new deal in just one word, we’ll leave that to the man himself…

item.title: Brundle unconvinced Ferrari can stop another Hamilton-Leclerc clash
item.description: Martin Brundle expects another flashpoint between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc , warning that any internal talks within Ferrari following their clash in Mexico are unlikely to prevent a repeat. Ferrari missed out on a potential 1-2 after both drivers ran wide at Turn 4, when Leclerc challenged Hamilton for the lead. Max Verstappen capitalised to take the victory, with Hamilton finishing in P2 and Leclerc in P4. Brundle expects Ferrari to address the clash internally before this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix. However, he questioned whether any meeting would prevent a repeat situation between their two drivers. He told Sky Sports:"it doesn't look pretty for the team, it's like when Lando (Norris) ran into Oscar Piastri in Singapore in the sprint race, it doesn't look pretty for the team and you let 1,500 people down and that's just the car side. You let people down in your team, you are only the final link in the chain of your team but you are the one out there that's got to deliver in the heat of the moment. "So Ferrari will have to manage that somehow and they will sit down, we will go to Brazil, and they will say 'yes we've sat down and we understood it all, move forward, it won't happen again,' but in reality we know that it will. Brundle: Leclerc has had frustrations this year Brundle also told Sky Sports that there has been some frustration within the Ferrari camp this season, particularly on Leclerc's side. After dominating Hamilton in 2025, Leclerc, until now, has been outperformed more often than not by the seven-time world champion. Despite Hamilton's criticism of Leclerc after the Mexico City Grand Prix, Brundle defended Leclerc, with a reference to Ayrton Senna's famous quote about not going for a gap which is there. He said: "You know what? They’re hardwired racing drivers. It’s a curious business we have where you perform as an individual totally in a team environment. You’re measured as an individual, you’re rewarded as an individual. “And then when the adrenaline’s up and the chance of the gap is there, as the great Ayrton Senna said, ‘If you don’t go for a gap, you’re no longer a racing driver.’ And that’s what they did. There’s some frustration. Charles had some frustrations this year."

He said: "You know what? They’re hardwired racing drivers. It’s a curious business we have where you perform as an individual totally in a team environment. You’re measured as an individual, you’re rewarded as an individual. “And then when the adrenaline’s up and the chance of the gap is there, as the great Ayrton Senna said, ‘If you don’t go for a gap, you’re no longer a racing driver.’ And that’s what they did. There’s some frustration. Charles had some frustrations this year."

item.title: Fan Letters: ‘We Need To Get Behind The Manager And The Lads’
item.description: Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris watches the Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light in Sunderland, on October 25, 2026. (Photo by Michael Driver/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Dear Roker Report We need to get behind the manager and the Lads. We’ve seen what constant change looks like, and it hasn’t exactly been a roaring success. New managers, new philosophies, rebuilding the squad every 12 months. At some point, you have to trust the process and give people time to develop. We’ve spent years demanding a long-term plan, but some supporters seem unwilling to tolerate the patience required to make one work. Getting Brobbey and Ballard back are big steps in the right direction. Injuries and a harsh hand from the fixture computer have contributed to the position we sit in the table. Yes, the players and the manager could also do better, but something positive is just around the corner. Let’s not end up like the shower up the road, who boo their team off the park at half-time and full-time. We’re better than that. Steve, Washington Editor’s note [Martin] Thanks for the email Steve. We’ve all seen what happens when we don’t have stability – no one wants to go back to those days. Similarly, I’m sure the vast majority of us want Regis Le Bris to enjoy more and more success here. Change doesn’t automatically mean things are going to go well – nor does it mean they’re going to go badly. Le Bris staying doesn’t guarantee either of those either. We can all see where we need to improve, and the reality is the players’ performance hasn’t been good enough this season, and neither have results. The ideal is Le Bris is able to change that – the question is how long can the club wait for things to change? I believe the playing squad is more than capable of competing towards the top third of the league, and I suspect the club believe that too. So putting sentiment and the past to one side, he needs to start getting results over the next couple of months, or he’ll be replaced. Dear Roker Report I think Sunderland supporters should give credit where it’s due for what Régis has done over the three years he’s been with us. After all, look how long it took Sir Alex Ferguson to get there when he was manager. So come on, supporters, give Régis a chance. He’s the best manager we’ve had in years. Ian Frame Editor’s note [Martin] Thanks for the email Ian. I don’t think anyone would fail to give Le Bris credit for what he’s achieved in the 2 seasons he’s had here. Hopefully he’ll turn this situation around – however if a new manager had come in in the summer and the team was producing this level of performance and results he’d likely already have gone. Football moves quickly, it’s a results business, you know the cliches, and if things don’t drastically pick up soon we’ll be in massive trouble. item.title: What’s The Root Cause Of Sunderland’s Current Struggles?
item.description: Regis Le Bris, manager of Sunderland AFC, looks on during the Carabao Cup Round of 16 match between Sunderland and Brentford at the Stadium of Light in Sunderland, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Kevin Hodgson/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images As we sit looking up at the rest of the table, it’s fair to ask why. Either the recruitment has failed, or the coach is at fault. If the players lack confidence, make basic errors or are simply out of form, it’s the coach’s job to correct it. ​Starting with recruitment, let’s look back at the summer’s business. Most supporters seemed to agree on what we needed: a left back, cover for Granit Xhaka, a right and left winger, a third forward and possibly a centre half. ​Left back and Xhaka’s backup? Check, and it looks like we have a real find on our hands with Jules Ahoka. A central defender? Success again, and we collected an unexpected bonus in Thomas Meunier. ​The recruitment team succeeded with the acquisition of a left winger but failed to secure someone to operate on the right. I’m not going to criticise the failure to find someone ready to play an understudy role to Brian Brobbey, as that was always a big ask. We brought in one for the future in Juan Angulo and realistically, that’s all we could expect. ​So, ultimately we failed with the right winger, that’s all. The key question is: would Regis Le Bris have played with two wingers if they were available? I have my doubts. ​A quick review of our ten most expensive signings shows four of them are wingers (Malick Fofana, Simon Adingra, Nilson Angulo and Chemesdine Talbi). All are still on the club’s books, with Talbi recording the most Premier League starts with twenty to date. Adingra (ten starts) has been shipped out on loan and there’s obviously an issue with Talbi. This leaves Angulo (sixteen starts) as the only one consistently getting a game, as Fofana has hardly featured in the league. ​Some might point to inexperience, but the evidence shows otherwise. Around 30% of current Premier League footballers are under twenty three, so age is not the issue. Angulo appears to be the current favourite for the left-wing role but is the most inexperienced. ​Adingra had over sixty Premier League appearances and was an Ivory Coast international when he joined Sunderland. Talbi was less experienced but a Moroccan international with thirty appearances in the Belgian Pro League. Fofana had made over fifty appearances in Ligue 1 and a further fifty in the Belgian Pro League to his name when he was recruited. ​Four wingers at a combined cost of £92 million, with one a regular starter and the rest bit-part players, is not a good return. Nine games in, Fofana is still not a regular starter, and his situation has finally convinced me the ongoing problem with our wingers isn’t recruitment — it’s the coach. ​It’s true that Fofana has been asked to rapidly bed in with a new team and get used to a radically different league, but I’m sorry, that’s
item.content:encoded: Regis Le Bris, manager of Sunderland AFC, looks on during the Carabao Cup Round of 16 match between Sunderland and Brentford at the Stadium of Light in Sunderland, on October 28, 2026. (Photo by Kevin Hodgson/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images As we sit looking up at the rest of the table, it’s fair to ask why. Either the recruitment has failed, or the coach is at fault. If the players lack confidence, make basic errors or are simply out of form, it’s the coach’s job to correct it. ​Starting with recruitment, let’s look back at the summer’s business. Most supporters seemed to agree on what we needed: a left back, cover for Granit Xhaka, a right and left winger, a third forward and possibly a centre half. ​Left back and Xhaka’s backup? Check, and it looks like we have a real find on our hands with Jules Ahoka. A central defender? Success again, and we collected an unexpected bonus in Thomas Meunier. ​The recruitment team succeeded with the acquisition of a left winger but failed to secure someone to operate on the right. I’m not going to criticise the failure to find someone ready to play an understudy role to Brian Brobbey, as that was always a big ask. We brought in one for the future in Juan Angulo and realistically, that’s all we could expect. ​So, ultimately we failed with the right winger, that’s all. The key question is: would Regis Le Bris have played with two wingers if they were available? I have my doubts. ​A quick review of our ten most expensive signings shows four of them are wingers (Malick Fofana, Simon Adingra, Nilson Angulo and Chemesdine Talbi). All are still on the club’s books, with Talbi recording the most Premier League starts with twenty to date. Adingra (ten starts) has been shipped out on loan and there’s obviously an issue with Talbi. This leaves Angulo (sixteen starts) as the only one consistently getting a game, as Fofana has hardly featured in the league. ​Some might point to inexperience, but the evidence shows otherwise. Around 30% of current Premier League footballers are under twenty three, so age is not the issue. Angulo appears to be the current favourite for the left-wing role but is the most inexperienced. ​Adingra had over sixty Premier League appearances and was an Ivory Coast international when he joined Sunderland. Talbi was less experienced but a Moroccan international with thirty appearances in the Belgian Pro League. Fofana had made over fifty appearances in Ligue 1 and a further fifty in the Belgian Pro League to his name when he was recruited. ​Four wingers at a combined cost of £92 million, with one a regular starter and the rest bit-part players, is not a good return. Nine games in, Fofana is still not a regular starter, and his situation has finally convinced me the ongoing problem with our wingers isn’t recruitment — it’s the coach. ​It’s true that Fofana has been asked to rapidly bed in with a new team and get used to a radically different league, but I’m sorry, that’s the nature of the beast. On a human level, football is a brutal game and whatever the circumstances, players have to step up and perform. It’s that simple. ​Arsenal were apparently interested in Fofana’s services. Crystal Palace certainly were, so what’s happened and why is it not working? Sorry, but that’s down to the coaching and/or tactics. Again, I’m being harsh but I suspect Régis Le Bris’ current tactics would make Jeremy Doku look average. ​Now to midfield — the nub of the issue. Xhaka has been poor and that in turn has dragged down the performance levels of Noah Sadiki in particular, but also Enzo Le Fée. I am going to given the recruitment some criticism here and suggest they should have been ready for that possibility given Xhaka’s age and the impact of the Chelsea nonsense. They should have had a ready-to-go replacement. That said, Ahoka should be getting more game time, and that’s down to the coach. ​Finally, there is the defence, and I don’t believe there’s been a failure of recruitment there. We have five proven central defenders and one (Meunier) who could play there if needed. It’s true one centre half has a relatively long-term injury and two are badly out of form, but how many centre halves are we expected to carry in the squad? Is poor form down to the recruitment or the coach? ​Some might claim we lack flair players, but I disagree. First, as evidence to the court, I present Le Fée — enough said. I’ve already covered the winger situation, but to compound the baffling Talbi exclusion, he’s shown that he can be a threat when used as an attacking ten, and Chris Rigg could be a lot more expansive if given the opportunity. ​Habib Diarra would be classed as a ‘flair player’ if he could play more than five minutes without breaking down. As our most expensive player, I assume the coach had a significant input into his signing, so if he were available, where would he play? ​We’ll have to wait and see what happens if Diarra is available for an extended period, but currently I don’t see Le Bris using him in the free-flowing attacking role that plays to his strengths. ​For example, I suggest Diarra could play as an attacking ten. He could be a Kevin Phillips-type ten, playing off a big man (not quite as tall as Niall Quinn but about twice as wide). It would mean moving Le Fée but it would be an option, and Talbi could even fill that role as a backup. ​Can I see Le Bris considering such an admittedly radical option, or any other option that diverges significantly from the current team structure? No, and that’s a problem. Something needs to change because if he persists with the current approach, it’s not going to end well. ​To be fair to the recruitment team, the options are there but most involve more than minor tweaks. Can Le Bris find the answers? I really hope so, and he certainly deserves the backing to try.

item.title: 4 Biggest Takeaways From Rangers’ Win Over Blues
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The New York Rangers secured a 3-1 win over the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday night, snapping a four-game losing streak in the process. Here are some of the main takeaways from the Rangers’ victory: Dylan Garand Bounces Back: Leading into Tuesday night, Garand had started eight of the Rangers’ nine games in the wake of Igor Shesterkin’s season-ending injury, and the cracks in his game were beginning to show as his workload continued to mount and fatigue set in. After the team’s 4-1 loss to the Edmonton Oilers on Sunday night, Garand was critical of himself, putting the blame solely on his shoulders. “Honestly, inexcusable,” Garand said of his performance on Sunday night. “Let the guys down. Pretty disappointing, put that loss on me. And yeah, it sucks.” The 24-year-old goaltender bounced back in a big way against the Blues, making 32 saves on 33 shots. Over the course of the night, Garand made some timely stops whenever the Blues gained offensive momentum, and he appeared to be steadier and more composed in his crease. “I just felt good,” Garand said. “I just really tried not to think out there. I think I've been doing too much of that lately in my game, so I just tried to go out there and battle and stop pucks.” Going into the night, Garand was facing scrutiny, with his game beginning to go in the wrong direction after a strong start to the season. However, his near-shutout performance helped keep the Rangers afloat throughout the contest and ultimately helped propel them to a much-needed victory. Mike Sullivan has been most impressed with Garand’s mental toughness and resilience through difficult times. “I think this game was an important one for him,” Sullivan said of Garand. “He wanted to bounce back and have a solid night for the group, and he did. I think his resilience, just his ability to move by circumstances and not not let it affect his performance or his game moving forward… I think that's a maturity that I've certainly witnessed in the short time that I've been around him. I think he’s proven what he’s capable of.” Will Cuylle Thrives At Center: Sullivan decided to tweak his lines going into Tuesday night’s matchup, with the biggest change revolving around putting Cuylle at the center position. Cuylle had never played center at any level of hockey, but Sullivan believed his skills translated well to playing down the middle. “I just feel like where we're at, we need to affect a little bit of change,” Sullivan said. “Will has a lot of qualities or the attributes that I think would allow him to be effective at that position. He can skate, he has good size, he can lean on people down low.” Anchoring the Rangers’ third line alongside Oliver Bjorkstrand and Eeli Tolvanen, Cuylle looked natural at center while continuing to play the same physical, hard-forechecking game we’ve grown accustomed to seeing from him. “I was excited before the game,” Cuylle said. “Obviously, a challenge for me, something I've never done. item.content:encoded: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The New York Rangers secured a 3-1 win over the St. Louis Blues on Tuesday night, snapping a four-game losing streak in the process. Here are some of the main takeaways from the Rangers’ victory: Dylan Garand Bounces Back: Leading into Tuesday night, Garand had started eight of the Rangers’ nine games in the wake of Igor Shesterkin’s season-ending injury, and the cracks in his game were beginning to show as his workload continued to mount and fatigue set in. After the team’s 4-1 loss to the Edmonton Oilers on Sunday night, Garand was critical of himself, putting the blame solely on his shoulders. “Honestly, inexcusable,” Garand said of his performance on Sunday night. “Let the guys down. Pretty disappointing, put that loss on me. And yeah, it sucks.” The 24-year-old goaltender bounced back in a big way against the Blues, making 32 saves on 33 shots. Over the course of the night, Garand made some timely stops whenever the Blues gained offensive momentum, and he appeared to be steadier and more composed in his crease. “I just felt good,” Garand said. “I just really tried not to think out there. I think I've been doing too much of that lately in my game, so I just tried to go out there and battle and stop pucks.” Going into the night, Garand was facing scrutiny, with his game beginning to go in the wrong direction after a strong start to the season. However, his near-shutout performance helped keep the Rangers afloat throughout the contest and ultimately helped propel them to a much-needed victory. Mike Sullivan has been most impressed with Garand’s mental toughness and resilience through difficult times. “I think this game was an important one for him,” Sullivan said of Garand. “He wanted to bounce back and have a solid night for the group, and he did. I think his resilience, just his ability to move by circumstances and not not let it affect his performance or his game moving forward… I think that's a maturity that I've certainly witnessed in the short time that I've been around him. I think he’s proven what he’s capable of.” Will Cuylle Thrives At Center: Sullivan decided to tweak his lines going into Tuesday night’s matchup, with the biggest change revolving around putting Cuylle at the center position. Cuylle had never played center at any level of hockey, but Sullivan believed his skills translated well to playing down the middle. “I just feel like where we're at, we need to affect a little bit of change,” Sullivan said. “Will has a lot of qualities or the attributes that I think would allow him to be effective at that position. He can skate, he has good size, he can lean on people down low.” Anchoring the Rangers’ third line alongside Oliver Bjorkstrand and Eeli Tolvanen, Cuylle looked natural at center while continuing to play the same physical, hard-forechecking game we’ve grown accustomed to seeing from him. “I was excited before the game,” Cuylle said. “Obviously, a challenge for me, something I've never done. Kind of felt a little nervous before the game, but after first couple shifts, settled in and just felt like myself.” Cuylle created an offensive-zone turnover in the third period, which helped lead to a goal from Bjorkstrand, giving the Rangers a 2-0 lead. Playing on both the power play and penalty kill, Cuylle logged a total of 18:19, the third-most among all Rangers forwards. The switch to center, on top of his usage in critical situations, shows Sullivan’s evolving trust in Cuylle as he continues to develop his game. “I thought he played real well. I thought he had a comfort level there. I liked what I saw,” Sullivan said of Cuylle’s performance playing center. Rangers' New-Look Fourth Line Provides Energy: The Blueshirts came into this game with quite a few line changes, including forming a new-look fourth line featuring Jaroslav Chmelař, Noah Laba, and Matt Rempe. All three players had a lot to prove. Chmelař was called up from the Hartford Wolf Pack of the American Hockey League just one day before, hungry to etch his mark in the NHL. Laba was moved down to the fourth line after Sullivan called his overall game a “mixed bag,” and Rempe had only been in the lineup for two of the Rangers’ previous 15 games. The newly assembled trio provided the Rangers with energy that the team has not gotten from its fourth line for much of the season. They were able to spend a large chunk of their shifts in the offensive zone, generating offense in the process while using their physicality well at both ends of the ice. “I thought they had a really solid game for us,” Sullivan said of the fourth line. “Labs and Jaro can really skate. I think they add a lot of pace to that line, and Remps obviously with his size and his reach and his and his aggressiveness. “I thought they had some really good momentum shifts for us. They spent a significant amount of time in the offensive zone. They had a couple of scoring opportunities, but the biggest thing that that line can bring to the team I think is just helping us create momentum with their physical play.” Since Joe Veleno went down with a lower-body injury, Sullivan has kept his fourth line on a short leash. However, he seemed to find a rhythm on Tuesday night, deploying the fourth line more frequently, with both Chmelař and Rempe playing over eight minutes despite not seeing any time on special teams. Scott Morrow Showing Improvement: Despite making the Rangers’ opening-night roster out of training camp, Scott Morrow served as a healthy scratch over the team’s first 14 games of the season. “I wouldn’t call it difficult necessarily,” Morrow said on not playing at all to start the season. “I feel blessed to be here, be a part of this group. Just trying to stay ready, have a positive attitude, and be ready for my chance to play.” A lower-body injury to Sean Durzi has given Morrow a chance to step into the lineup, and he’s been able to seize this opportunity. In two games, the 24-year-old defenseman has continued to flash his impressive puckhandling abilities, quick skating, and offensive instincts, skills we already knew were in his wheelhouse. However, what’s been a surprise is his improved defensive play. Morrow struggled to defend at a consistent level last year, one of the biggest reasons he spent a large chunk of the 2025-26 season playing in the American Hockey League. However, he’s shown heightened awareness from a defensive standpoint over this short two-game sample size. “Scotty has played well,” Sullivan said. “I think his pace is better. I think he's quicker. He's closing on people. I think his stick detail, just disrupting plays, getting his stick on the puck, things of that nature. I think that continues to evolve and improve and get better. I think he's making pretty good reads defensively. I know Scotty is making a real concerted effort on the defensive side of the puck to try to continue to evolve and improve.”

item.title: NIMASA threatens sanctions over missing marine incident reports
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has threatened sanctions against Port Facility Security Officers (PFSOs) who fail to properly report marine security incidents, warning that bypassing approved reporting channels constitutes a breach of international port security rules. The warning followed concerns that incident reports from port facilities were being sent to individual NIMASA officials instead of the agency’s designated International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Unit. In a notice signed by Mudi Isa, Head, ISPS Code Unit, the agency directed all PFSOs to route incident reports through the approved ISPS Unit email address. The notice, titled “Non-Receipt of Incident Reports/Submission to Approved ISPS Unit,” said: “It has come to our attention that the Unit is currently not receiving your incident report emails, which poses a significant risk.” NIMASA warned that the failure to use the prescribed channel could have serious implications for maritime security. “Failure to report security incidents to the correct channels constitutes a breach of ISPS compliance,” it stated. The agency specifically directed port facility security personnel to stop sending or copying reports to individual NIMASA staff emails unless expressly authorised. “Do not copy or send reports to individual staff emails unless explicitly authorised,” the notice stated. NIMASA also directed PFSOs to confirm receipt of every incident report and contact the ISPS Unit immediately if no acknowledgement was received within 24 hours. “If you do not receive an acknowledgment from the ISPS Unit within 24hrs of submission, contact the Unit immediately via phone,” it said. The agency further advised operators who were unsure of the approved reporting directory to contact the ISPS Unit for verification before submitting their reports. NIMASA said the directive was aimed at ensuring that security incidents and anomalies are captured promptly and handled through a coordinated response mechanism. item.dc:creator: Urowayino Jeremiah
item.content:encoded: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has threatened sanctions against Port Facility Security Officers (PFSOs) who fail to properly report marine security incidents, warning that bypassing approved reporting channels constitutes a breach of international port security rules. The warning followed concerns that incident reports from port facilities were being sent to individual NIMASA officials instead of the agency’s designated International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Unit. In a notice signed by Mudi Isa, Head, ISPS Code Unit, the agency directed all PFSOs to route incident reports through the approved ISPS Unit email address. The notice, titled “Non-Receipt of Incident Reports/Submission to Approved ISPS Unit,” said: “It has come to our attention that the Unit is currently not receiving your incident report emails, which poses a significant risk.” NIMASA warned that the failure to use the prescribed channel could have serious implications for maritime security. “Failure to report security incidents to the correct channels constitutes a breach of ISPS compliance,” it stated. The agency specifically directed port facility security personnel to stop sending or copying reports to individual NIMASA staff emails unless expressly authorised. “Do not copy or send reports to individual staff emails unless explicitly authorised,” the notice stated. NIMASA also directed PFSOs to confirm receipt of every incident report and contact the ISPS Unit immediately if no acknowledgement was received within 24 hours. “If you do not receive an acknowledgment from the ISPS Unit within 24hrs of submission, contact the Unit immediately via phone,” it said. The agency further advised operators who were unsure of the approved reporting directory to contact the ISPS Unit for verification before submitting their reports. NIMASA said the directive was aimed at ensuring that security incidents and anomalies are captured promptly and handled through a coordinated response mechanism. item.title: Rams QB Matthew Stafford’s wife rips NFL on Instagram for bye week schedule quirk
item.description: Rams QB Matthew Stafford’s wife rips NFL on Instagram for bye week schedule quirk appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams have a relatively short bye week coming up, a scheduling decision that hasn’t sat well with quarterback Matthew Stafford ’s wife, Kelly, who made her displeasure with the NFL public. In an Instagram Story posted on Tuesday, Kelly tagged the league’s official account and questioned why Los Angeles is the only team without a traditional bye week , seeking an explanation for the shortened break. “Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week,” wrote Kelly. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) She also brought some humor into her criticism, pointing out that even after spending 18 years around professional football, she needs a break despite never having played a snap. “Because after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap. I’m tired just watching from the stands. Can’t imagine how the guys feel.” Moreover, Kelly invited the NFL to respond about its scheduling decision by adding a question box. The Rams technically have a Week 11 bye, but their schedule gives them considerably less time away from competition than a conventional midseason break. Los Angeles will face the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, November 15, before returning to the field against the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday, November 25. The matchup will be the league’s first Thanksgiving Eve game and will be played at SoFi Stadium, with Netflix carrying the broadcast. Instead of receiving the usual two-week gap between games, the Rams will have just 10 days between their Cardinals and Packers matchups. Green Bay, meanwhile, will have a more favorable arrangement after the Thanksgiving Eve contest. The team will immediately enter its bye week and will not play again until December 6. Los Angeles’ demanding schedule extends beyond its shortened break. The Rams are projected to travel 34,847 miles during the season, making them the NFL’s second-most-traveled team behind the San Francisco 49ers, who are scheduled to cover 38,105 miles. Both NFC West rivals opened their campaigns in Melbourne, Australia, on September 10. The Rams have several challenging matchups remaining. Following their Packers game, they will have eight days before facing the Kansas City Chiefs on December 3. Their remaining schedule includes games against the 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks and Tampa Bay Buccaneers before a season-ending home matchup versus the Seahawks. Related: Rams HC Sean McVay provides key Myles Garrett injury update before Commanders clash Related: Rams’ Trent McDuffie gets positive update from Sean McVay amid injury concerns

item.title: Nigeria’s exports record 25% increase in 2yrs — NPA
item.description: By Godwin Oritse Nigeria’s exports have increased by 25 per cent in the last two years, driven by Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port terminal operators, the Managing Director of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, has said. Speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH), Dantsoho said the growth covered both oil and non-oil exports. “For us in Nigeria, the most important thing is that we are seeing growth as a result of this policy that we are taking. Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. “These are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In manufacturing and agriculture, raw materials like cocoa and cashew, volumes have increased, and that is to the credit of the partnership between ourselves and the major terminal operators, APM Terminals,” he said. He attributed the improvement to Export Processing Terminals established by the NPA. “We have got about four of those in Nigeria where we collaborate with the terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other agencies that have a stake, so that everything regarding the processing of cargo for export is done locally,” he stated. On the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), Dantsoho said: “Nigeria’s economy is very strong now because of our president’s reforms, which everyone can testify is attracting investors to the country.” He added that port reforms had improved operational efficiency and increased revenue. “We have experienced a lot of increase in volumes and revenue that has been generated by the ports across Nigeria. As a matter of fact, the efficiency in the ports in Nigeria is far better now than those of other West African countries,” he said. Dantsoho also disclosed that the Federal Government was investing $1 billion in expanding and modernising Apapa Port, with private-sector partnerships supporting infrastructure and technology development. item.title: US Midterms: Trump accepts midterm results, pledges to work with Democrats
item.description: United States President Donald Trump has said he is prepared to accept the outcome of the country’s midterm elections and work with Democrats, as results showed the opposition party heading towards control of both chambers of Congress. Trump made the remarks on Tuesday night during a telephone interview with The New York Times, as he monitored election results at the White House. “We’ll, you know, look forward to working with them,” he said. “We’ll probably work something out.” The President’s comments came amid major Republican losses, with Democrats making significant gains in closely contested races and threatening Republican control of Congress. Trump attributed his party’s poor performance partly to his absence from the ballot, suggesting that his participation could have changed the outcome. He also defended his decision to launch a war against Iran, describing it as a “very wise decision”. The President further said he had no regrets about endorsing Republican candidates, including South Carolina Senator Darline Graham and Texas Attorney-General Ken Paxton, who both lost their Senate bids. Speaking shortly before 10:30pm on Tuesday, Trump said he was following the election results during the interview. “I’m just looking at these results as I’m talking,” he said. Reacting to Graham’s defeat, he added: “I see that Darline lost. Wow, that’s amazing. How do you think Lindsey would have done if he ran?” He was referring to Senator Lindsey Graham, who reportedly died in July. Democrats were on course to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate as results continued to emerge, PUNCH Online had reported on Wednesday. A Democratic takeover of Congress would significantly alter the balance of political power in Washington, potentially subjecting Trump’s administration to increased congressional scrutiny and making it more difficult for the President to advance his legislative agenda during the remaining two years of his term. Vanguard Newspaper The post US Midterms: Trump accepts midterm results, pledges to work with Democrats appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ADC accuses Sokoto govt of intimidation, demands reopening of campaign office
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused the Sokoto State Government of using the police to intimidate opposition politicians and frustrate its political activities, following the sealing of its state campaign office in Sokoto. The party demanded the immediate reopening of the premises, describing the action as illegal and an infringement on its constitutional rights ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the ADC said its campaign office along Ahmadu Bello Way in Sokoto metropolis was sealed on Tuesday, November 3, by officers of the Sokoto State Police Command allegedly acting on the orders of the state government. The development occurred barely hours before the commencement of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in the state, with the proposed campaign venue reportedly remaining locked. The statement was signed by Yusuf Suleiman, also known as Dan Amar Sokoto, Deputy Director-General of Administration of the Atiku Abubakar ADC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, and made available to journalists. The party alleged that the premises were sealed without a court order, prior notice or any lawful explanation from the authorities. It described the action as “illegal, unconstitutional and reckless”, arguing that it violated its rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and political participation. The ADC also cited Section 95 of the Electoral Act 2026, arguing that the action undermined the legal protections available to registered political parties to organise and conduct their activities without unlawful interference. The party further linked the development to what it described as a pattern of political intimidation in the state, recalling an alleged attack on its governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at Sultan Sadiq Abubakar International Airport four days earlier. It dismissed suggestions that the authorities might not have known who occupied the building, insisting that the party had operated openly from the premises for more than eight years. “The claim that the authorities do not know who occupies the building is not credible. The ADC has operated openly from those premises for more than eight years,” the statement said. The party argued that any genuine inquiry into the ownership or occupation of the property should have been made through a formal letter rather than the deployment of armed police officers to seal its premises. It also alleged that the state government was concerned about the growing support for the ADC and its candidates, accusing it of responding to political competition with force rather than democratic engagement. “We reject this conduct in its entirety. We will pursue every legitimate and lawful remedy available to us to reopen our office and to protect our members, our supporters and our property in Sokoto,” it stated. The party demanded the immediate reopening of the premises, describing the action as illegal and an infringement on its constitutional rights ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the ADC said its campaign office along Ahmadu Bello Way in Sokoto metropolis was sealed on Tuesday, November 3, by officers of the Sokoto State Police Command allegedly acting on the orders of the state government. The development occurred barely hours before the commencement of the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in the state, with the proposed campaign venue reportedly remaining locked. The statement was signed by Yusuf Suleiman, also known as Dan Amar Sokoto, Deputy Director-General of Administration of the Atiku Abubakar ADC 2027 Presidential Campaign Council, and made available to journalists. The party alleged that the premises were sealed without a court order, prior notice or any lawful explanation from the authorities. It described the action as “illegal, unconstitutional and reckless”, arguing that it violated its rights to freedom of association, peaceful assembly and political participation. The ADC also cited Section 95 of the Electoral Act 2026, arguing that the action undermined the legal protections available to registered political parties to organise and conduct their activities without unlawful interference. The party further linked the development to what it described as a pattern of political intimidation in the state, recalling an alleged attack on its governorship candidate, Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, at Sultan Sadiq Abubakar International Airport four days earlier. It dismissed suggestions that the authorities might not have known who occupied the building, insisting that the party had operated openly from the premises for more than eight years. “The claim that the authorities do not know who occupies the building is not credible. The ADC has operated openly from those premises for more than eight years,” the statement said. The party argued that any genuine inquiry into the ownership or occupation of the property should have been made through a formal letter rather than the deployment of armed police officers to seal its premises. It also alleged that the state government was concerned about the growing support for the ADC and its candidates, accusing it of responding to political competition with force rather than democratic engagement. “We reject this conduct in its entirety. We will pursue every legitimate and lawful remedy available to us to reopen our office and to protect our members, our supporters and our property in Sokoto,” it stated. The ADC held the state government and the police command responsible for any breach of peace that might arise from the closure. It consequently called on the Inspector-General of Police to direct the immediate reopening of the premises and ensure that the police discharged their responsibilities impartially towards all political parties. The party also appealed to civil society organisations, election observers and the international community to condemn the action and demand explanations from the Sokoto State Government and the police. It specifically urged Nigeria’s international partners, including the United States, United Kingdom, European Union, France, Germany, Italy and the Commonwealth, to take note of what it described as actions undermining democratic governance in the state and consider visa restrictions against individuals found responsible for subverting democratic processes. “Democracy in Sokoto will not be locked away. The people of Sokoto will be heard,” the party declared. Vanguard Newspaper The post ADC accuses Sokoto govt of intimidation, demands reopening of campaign office appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: LG reinforces leadership in refrigerator market with Brandcom award
item.description: LG Electronics has strengthened its position in Nigeria’s home appliance market following the recognition of its MoodUP Refrigerator at the BRANDCOM awards 2026 in Lagos. The award recognises the refrigerator’s distinctive design and smart features, including customisable LED door panels and smart connectivity, which allow users to personalise their kitchen experience. Beyond its aesthetics, LG’s refrigerator range addresses practical household needs such as food preservation, energy efficiency and durability, which remain important considerations for Nigerian consumers. The company offers top-freezer, bottom-freezer, side-by-side and premium refrigerator models designed to accommodate different household sizes and lifestyles. One of its products, the GN-F452PFAQ Top Freezer Refrigerator, features FRESH Converter+ technology, which allows users to adjust temperature settings to suit different food types and maintain optimal freshness. It also comes with an automatic ice maker for added convenience. Selected LG refrigerator models are equipped with Smart Inverter Compressor , LINEARCooling and DoorCooling+ technologies, designed to improve energy efficiency, provide consistent cooling and preserve food freshness for longer. These features are particularly relevant to households seeking reliable refrigeration, lower energy consumption and dependable appliance performance. The recognition at the BRANDCOM Awards further highlights LG’s presence in Nigeria’s competitive refrigerator market. The post LG reinforces leadership in refrigerator market with Brandcom award appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mackinaw City, NMCA advance to MHSAA district volleyball finals
item.description: MACKINAW CITY — Mackinaw City will play for an MHSAA Division 4 district volleyball title . Taking on Mackinac Island in a district semifinal , the Comets booked their ticket to a championship clash at St. Ignace by capturing a 3-0 victory (25-12, 25-11, 25-16) over the Lakers in Mackinaw City on Tuesday, Nov. 3. MACK CITY'S RIAN ESPER: Esper a key Mackinaw City volleyball player in many different spots MACK CITY BOYS QUALIFY FOR XC STATES: Area's top performers paced by state-qualifier Mackinaw City boys XC DISTRICT VOLLEYBALL PREVIEW: Previewing, predicting Cheboygan-area volleyball district tournaments After starting slow and trailing 7-1 in the first set, the Comets (13-22-5) regrouped, battled back and took a one-set lead in the match. From there, they were in cruise control behind quality offensive and defensive play. "Once we were able to get ourselves settled, we played some very solid volleyball tonight and did a great job of getting into our system offensively, and our defense did a great job of digging balls and keeping balls alive to give ourselves a shot at winning some long volleys," Mackinaw City coach Jake Huffman said. Rian Esper's 10 kills, six aces and six digs fueled the Comets, who received 16 assists, seven digs, two kills and seven digs from Julia Short, and 11 digs, six assists, four kills and three aces from Emily Kruczynski. Mackinaw City's many other contributors included Alaia Mendez (eight kills, five aces, four digs), Poppy Wallace (five kills, two digs, one block), Ella Kruczynski (six aces, five digs, one assist), and Sarah Lentell (two kills, one dig). "I was very happy with our response and proud of the effort that ladies put forth tonight," Huffman said. "We will use (Wednesday) to prep for a very tough St. Ignace squad on Thursday." Thursday's district final at St. Ignace (10-11-7) is a 6 p.m. start. Eagles beat Alanson, will meet Harbor Light for title HARBOR SPRINGS — Get ready for a Northern Lakes Conference showdown for the district title on Thursday. Opening its postseason in style was the Burt Lake Northern Michigan Christian Academy volleyball team, which earned a 3-0 victory over Alanson (25-17, 25-10, 25-15) in an MHSAA Division 4 semifinal at Harbor Light on Tuesday, Nov. 3. The Eagles (23-6-2) were led by Shanna Ferraiuolo, who finished with 21 kills and four digs, while Lauren Ferraiuolo tallied 18 kills, three aces and three digs, and Hazel Bowman added 38 assists and three aces. Isabel Hoffmeyer chipped in with 12 digs. "Always nice to get a postseason win," NMCA coach Josh Ferraiuolo said. "We were a little rusty after being off for more than a week, but overall, we played pretty well. Looking forward to a very competitive final on Thursday." NMCA faces Harbor Light (16-6-6) in a 6 p.m. final on Thursday, Nov. 5, at Harbor Light. Harbor Light defeated Pellston 3-0 (25-14, 25-16, 25-7) in a semifinal on Tuesday. item.title: Caitlin Clark’s latest heartwarming gesture sees her send a massive gift to her alma mater
item.description: Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark had her former college team, the Iowa Hawkeyes, in mind after the Nike CC1 release. Clark dominated the NCAA with a four-year stint with the Hawkeyes. Although she never won a national championship, losing in the 2023 and 2024 finals, she set countless records for the college and the NCAA as a whole. Now with her third WNBA season in the rearview, Clark showed love to where she became a national superstar by sending a gift over to the current women’s basketball team on the Hawkeyes. Caitlin Clark gifts CC1s to Iowa Hawkeyes women’s basketball team Clark sent over custom black-and-gold Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoes to the Hawkeyes, creating a player-exclusive Iowa PE colorway for their season-opener against Towson. The team shared a video of the excited reactions current players had to the gift. The Hawkeyes also shared an in-game picture of how the sneakers looked on the players’ feet during the game. While Clark has previously gifted sneakers to the Hawkeyes team, including pairs of the CC1s, this is the first time she has created a team-exclusive PE for the players, featuring the University of Iowa Tigerhawk logo on the tongue. The Hawkeyes picked up a convincing 73-45 win over the Towson Tigers in their CBB season-opener on November 3. Junior Dani Carnegie, who was a freshman during Clark’s final year with the Hawkeyes, led them to the win with 21 points, five rebounds and five assists. Clark left the Hawkeyes without a championship, but set the NCAA Division 1 basketball scoring record with 2,951 points, breaking Pete Maravich’s 54-year-old 3,667-point record. She has also made the most three-pointers in NCAA history with 548, with her 201 threes in 23-24 setting the record for most in one season. Her legacy as a Hawkeye is arguably richer than any current professional athlete due to the historic nature of her four-year tenure. While not having a championship to cement it as the greatest NCAA career of all time is rough, she gave Iowa years of incredible basketball. Read more: What Caitlin Clark does that makes the rest of the WNBA ‘mad’ ‘Insane’ – Sophie Cunningham reacts to adults dressing as her for Halloween Caitlin Clark picks what was ‘the best part’ about the WNBA Finals series

item.title: Vikings’ Carson Wentz Gets Good News on Promotion Before Bills Game
item.description: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz. Getty The Minnesota Vikings won again in Week 7 arguably despite quarterback Kyler Murray. Getty The Vikings set Carson Wentz up for a big payday, but there is some strong doubts he will cash in. Getty Calls among Minnesota Vikings fans and media members who cover the team regularly are steadily growing for Kevin O’Connell to make a change under center from Kyler Murray to Carson Wentz, and the head coach may have just caught the break he needed to do so while still allowing the franchise to save face. The Vikings named Murray the starting QB over JJ McCarthy before either had taken a preseason snap. Minnesota then demoted McCarthy to QB3 before trading him to the New York Giants for a fifth-round draft asset in what was a fairly historic punt on top-10 pick in just his third NFL season at 23 years old and with only 10 starts on his resumé. Murray has not performed poorly enough that one can accurately call his season through seven games a worst-case scenario for the Vikings. But across the range of possible outcomes, Murray has definitely produced on the lower end of the spectrum. Benching him outright now would equate to O’Connell and first-year GM Nolan Teasley admitting that Murray’s elevation to QB1 and the team’s hastiness to sell low on McCarthy were both significant mistakes. However, Murray’s moderate hamstring concern, which he suffered in the team’s first loss of the season last week to the Detroit Lions , might be precisely the window O’Connell requires to go back to Wentz while maintaining plausible deniability with regards to Murray. Kyler Murray Suffered Hamstring Concern Last Week Getty Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray. O’Connell mentioned during the postgame that hamstring tightness was the reason for Murray’s trip to the blue tent on the sidelines during the fourth quarter in Detroit. On Tuesday, November 3, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reported that Murray could miss time due to the injury, which isn’t overly severe but may impact his ability to scramble. “I don’t get the sense it’s really bad, but he is a mobile QB,” Rapoport said . “If he can’t move like he needs to, then I don’t know that he’s gonna play.” Making plays with his legs has been Murray’s saving grace this season, and if he can’t do that effectively, it’s hard to imagine the Vikings scoring enough points to keep up with the visiting Buffalo Bills on next week’s addition of “Monday Night Football.” Vikings Arguably Soft-Benched JJ McCarthy for Carson Wentz Last Season Getty Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk wrote Tuesday that he suspects the Vikings will use Murray’s injury as “cover” for a “soft benching” that will allow O’Connell to go back to Wentz without formally demoting Murray. “It’s hard not to look at the current status of Murray’s hamstring ‘tightness’ as cover for a soft benching of Murray,” Florio wrote . “That gives the Vikings a chance to let Cars

Kyler Murray Suffered Hamstring Concern Last Week Getty Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray. O’Connell mentioned during the postgame that hamstring tightness was the reason for Murray’s trip to the blue tent on the sidelines during the fourth quarter in Detroit. On Tuesday, November 3, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reported that Murray could miss time due to the injury, which isn’t overly severe but may impact his ability to scramble. “I don’t get the sense it’s really bad, but he is a mobile QB,” Rapoport said . “If he can’t move like he needs to, then I don’t know that he’s gonna play.” Making plays with his legs has been Murray’s saving grace this season, and if he can’t do that effectively, it’s hard to imagine the Vikings scoring enough points to keep up with the visiting Buffalo Bills on next week’s addition of “Monday Night Football.” Vikings Arguably Soft-Benched JJ McCarthy for Carson Wentz Last Season Getty Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk wrote Tuesday that he suspects the Vikings will use Murray’s injury as “cover” for a “soft benching” that will allow O’Connell to go back to Wentz without formally demoting Murray. “It’s hard not to look at the current status of Murray’s hamstring ‘tightness’ as cover for a soft benching of Murray,” Florio wrote . “That gives the Vikings a chance to let Carson Wentz, who played well enough in most of the Week 1 win over the Packers and all of the Week 2 win over the Bears .” Several analysts suggested that Minnesota did essentially the same thing last season after McCarthy suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 2. Wentz stepped in, starting the next five games over a six-week span that included the Vikings’ bye. McCarthy eventually got the starting job back, though only after Wentz went down for the season with a shoulder injury that required surgery. If he had not suffered that injury when he did, circumstances would have forced the Vikings to tip their hand as to their true preferences at QB, with six weeks being the upward amount of time any player might legitimately miss with an ankle sprain — absent any setbacks.
